22:23.prayer: Lord, You see how easily I nest in comfort. Teach me that no height of ease can shelter me from every pain—but You can carry me through it. Be my refuge and peace. In Jesus' name, amen.

22:24.devotion: God swears by His own life that even if Coniah (Jehoiachin) were the precious signet ring on His hand, He would pluck him off. A signet represented authority and identity, yet unfaithful leadership would lose even that honored place. The verse teaches that closeness to God's favor is tied to faithfulness, not lineage or position.
22:24.reflection: Am I treasuring closeness to God, or assuming my background and roles secure His favor?
22:24.action: Thank God today for one way He has honored you, then ask Him to keep your heart faithful in that trust.
22:24.prayer: Gracious Lord, I don't want to hold any place in Your purposes carelessly. Keep me faithful, humble, and close to You, so my life stays in Your hand—not by merit or heritage, but by abiding in You. In Jesus' name, amen.

22:25.devotion: God speaks judgment to King Jehoiachin (Coniah) of Judah. Though he feared Babylon, the very power he dreaded would overcome him. His trust in politics and avoidance could not shield him from the consequences of a reign that ignored God's word. Even the feared cannot outrun God's justice.
22:25.reflection: When I am afraid of a person or power, where do I place my confidence and hope?
22:25.action: Name one fear you have been avoiding, and bring it honestly to God in prayer before the day ends.
22:25.prayer: Lord, You see every fear I carry, even the ones I hide from myself. Teach me to trust You more than the powers that intimidate me. Keep me faithful to Your word when it would be easier to please people. Amen.

22:26.devotion: Here God announces exile for Jehoiachin and his mother. The king who should have guarded Judah would be uprooted to a foreign land and die there. Leadership that abandons God's ways carries real consequences, not only for the leader but for those tied to him.
22:26.reflection: Are my choices today building a heritage of faithfulness, or am I sowing consequences others will reap with me?
22:26.action: Consider one decision you will make this week, and ask how it will affect the people connected to you.
22:26.prayer: Father, remind me that my life touches others. Help me lead wherever You place me with humility and obedience, so my influence blesses rather than burdens the people around me. Ground my days in Your ways. Amen.

22:27.devotion: The exiles longed to return home, but God declared that longing would go unfulfilled. When judgment fell because of persistent unfaithfulness, doors closed that might once have opened. This verse soberly shows that desires alone cannot reverse what God has determined.
22:27.reflection: Is there a longing in my life that I have pursued while ignoring what God has actually asked of me?
22:27.action: Write down one desire you have been chasing, and prayerfully ask God whether it aligns with His will for you.
22:27.prayer: Lord, You know the longings of my heart, some godly and some misplaced. Align my desires with Your purposes. Where I have chased what You have not given, teach me contentment and trust in Your wisdom. Amen.

22:28.devotion: Jeremiah poses a grief-stricken question: is Coniah a broken, despised vessel, cast away with his descendants into an unknown land? The once-enthroned king has become like shattered pottery, discarded. It is a lament over how far a leader and a nation can fall.
22:28.reflection: Do I treat my God-given roles as treasures to steward faithfully, or as things I can handle carelessly?
22:28.action: Identify one responsibility God has given you, and take one intentional step today to carry it out more faithfully.
22:28.prayer: Father, keep me from becoming a vessel set aside through neglect and disobedience. Whatever You have placed in my hands, help me honor it. Shape me into a life that is useful and pleasing to You. Amen.

22:29.devotion: The prophet calls three times: O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the LORD! The repetition is urgent and mournful, summoning all creation as a witness. God's declaration about the throne of David and the fate of Judah is not a casual word but one the whole world should heed.
22:29.reflection: Do I give God's word urgent, listening attention, or do I let it pass over me like background noise?
22:29.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes today to read Scripture slowly and listen, without phone or distraction.
22:29.prayer: Lord, You still speak, and Your word deserves my full attention. Slow me down from distraction and hurry. Give me ears that truly hear, and a heart that responds with obedience to what You say. Amen.

22:30.devotion: God commands that Jehoiachin be recorded as childless in the royal sense: none of his descendants would prosper sitting on David's throne in Judah. His line would not continue the kingship. This judgment ends his dynasty's rule, while God's larger promise to David remains His to fulfill in His own way.
22:30.reflection: Am I seeking lasting faithfulness before God, or only the visible success of my own days?
22:30.action: Reflect for a few minutes on what you most want remembered about your life, and choose one way to live that out today.
22:30.prayer: Father, You hold all history and every throne in Your hands. Keep me from chasing fleeting achievements. Let my life be marked by faithfulness to You, trusting You to accomplish what Your promises declare. Amen.

23:1.devotion: God pronounces woe on the shepherds, the leaders of Judah, who destroyed and scattered the sheep of His pasture. The people belong to God, not to the leaders. Those entrusted with care who instead harmed and neglected the flock face His direct rebuke. God takes the mistreatment of His people personally.
23:1.reflection: Where God has given me influence over others, am I caring for them or serving my own interests?
23:1.action: Think of one person under your care or influence, and do something concrete today for their genuine good.
23:1.prayer: Lord, You see how Your people are treated, and You defend them. Keep me from using others for my gain. Where I hold any responsibility, make me gentle, honest, and attentive, caring for people as Yours. Amen.

23:2.devotion: God declares He will attend to the shepherds who scattered His flock, drove them away, and failed to care for them. The same verb appears pointedly: they did not attend to the sheep, so He will attend to them. Negligent leadership will answer to the God who calls His people My flock.
23:2.reflection: Have I neglected a duty toward someone God placed near me, hoping no one would notice?
23:2.action: Choose one neglected responsibility toward another person and complete it today, however small it seems.
23:2.prayer: Father, You attend to every wrong done to Your people, and You see my failures too. Forgive my neglect where I have fallen short. Make me trustworthy in the small duties as well as the great ones. Amen.

23:3.devotion: Speaking against Judah's unfaithful leaders, God promises He will personally gather the scattered remnant of His flock from every country where they were driven. Though exile brought pain, His plan includes restoration, fruitfulness, and growth. His care for His people outlasts their worst seasons of loss.
23:3.reflection: Where do I need to trust that God can restore what feels scattered in my life?
23:3.action: Identify one area of loss or distance in your walk with God today, and write a short prayer asking Him to gather and renew it.
23:3.prayer: Good Shepherd, thank You that no distance can remove me from Your care. Gather the scattered pieces of my life, and make me fruitful where I have felt barren. I rest in Your promise of restoration. Amen.

23:4.devotion: After promising to regather His flock, God pledges to raise shepherds who will actually feed and care for them. Under such leadership, His people will no longer live in fear, dismay, or lack. This contrasts sharply with the negligent rulers of Jeremiah's day, showing God's heart for genuine pastoral care.
23:4.reflection: Am I praying for, and supporting, leaders who truly feed God's people rather than neglect them?
23:4.action: Send an encouraging note or message today to a pastor, teacher, or mentor who has faithfully cared for you spiritually.
23:4.prayer: Lord, thank You for caring shepherds who feed Your flock. Strengthen those who serve Your people well, correct leaders who harm, and help me be a grateful, encouraging part of Your church family. Amen.

23:5.devotion: In contrast to Judah's failed kings, God promises a coming Branch from David's line, a righteous King who will reign wisely, prosper, and carry out justice and righteousness in the earth. Christians see this promise fulfilled in Jesus, the true heir of David whose kingdom is marked by perfect justice.
23:5.reflection: How does it change my outlook to remember that the righteous King has already come and will reign fully?
23:5.action: Choose one situation today where fairness is needed, and act justly in it, even if no one else notices.
23:5.prayer: Faithful God, thank You for raising up the righteous Branch, Jesus, my King. When earth's leaders fail, help me anchor my hope in His justice and righteousness, and live today as a citizen of His kingdom. Amen.

23:6.devotion: This verse completes the promise of the coming King: in His days, Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell securely. His astonishing name, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS, reveals that our standing before God rests not on our own record but on the Lord Himself, who becomes righteousness for us.
23:6.reflection: Do I rest in righteousness given by the Lord, or keep trying to earn my standing before God?
23:6.action: Write out the name THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS somewhere visible today, and thank God each time you see it.
23:6.prayer: Lord, my righteousness, thank You that my acceptance with You rests on Christ, not my performance. Teach me to stop striving for approval and to live securely in the salvation You provide. Amen.

23:7.devotion: God declares that a day is coming when His people's praise will no longer center only on the exodus from Egypt. As great as that deliverance was, He is preparing an even greater act of rescue that will become the new focal point of their worship and testimony.
23:7.reflection: Which past deliverance am I still dwelling on when God wants to write a new story of rescue?
23:7.action: Share with someone today one way God has recently rescued, guided, or provided for you, however small it seems.
23:7.prayer: God of deliverance, thank You for every rescue in my past, and thank You that Your saving work is not finished. Open my eyes to see the new things You are doing in my life today. Amen.

23:8.devotion: The promised new confession will celebrate the Lord who brings His people home from the north country and all the nations where they were driven. The God who once delivered from Egypt would again gather, lead, and settle His people. Rescue would be personal, comprehensive, and complete.
23:8.reflection: Do I believe God can lead me home from whatever far country my circumstances or choices have taken me?
23:8.action: Pray specifically today for one person you know who has wandered far from God, asking Him to lead them back home.
23:8.prayer: Lord who leads Your people home, thank You that no place is too distant for Your gathering grace. Bring back the wandering ones I love, and lead me ever closer to Your presence. Amen.

23:9.devotion: Jeremiah describes his own anguish: his heart is broken, his bones shake, and he feels overcome, all because of the Lord and His holy words. Standing for truth in a corrupt time was not easy for the prophet. Faithfulness to God sometimes carries deep emotional cost.
23:9.reflection: When has telling or standing for the truth cost me something, and how did I respond to God in that moment?
23:9.action: If you have grown weary from standing for what is right, bring that weariness honestly to God in prayer today.
23:9.prayer: Lord of truth, thank You for Jeremiah's honest example. When obedience leaves me trembling or heartbroken, meet me in that pain, steady my heart, and remind me that Your holy words are worth every cost. Amen.

23:10.devotion: Jeremiah diagnoses the spiritual rot of his land: it is full of adulterers, the ground mourns under a curse, and even the wilderness is dried up. The people's strength is misused for evil. Jeremiah shows that unfaithfulness to God has consequences that spread through every part of life and land.
23:10.reflection: In what area of my life is my strength being used for myself rather than for God's good purposes?
23:10.action: Ask God today to search your heart for any unfaithfulness, then confess it and take one step of repentance.
23:10.prayer: Holy God, search my heart and show me where my strength serves the wrong purposes. Forgive my unfaithfulness, renew my devotion to You, and let my life water the ground around me rather than dry it. Amen.

23:11.devotion: Jeremiah speaks God's word against the spiritual leaders of Judah. The prophets and priests, who should have modeled holiness, had become corrupt—even in the temple itself, the very place dedicated to God's presence. Their unfaithfulness in sacred office made their guilt especially serious before the Lord.
23:11.reflection: Where might God be calling me to greater integrity in responsibilities He has entrusted to me?
23:11.action: Examine one area of duty today—work, family, or church—and honestly name any way you have fallen short before God.
23:11.prayer: Lord, search my heart. Keep me faithful in every role You have given me, and let my life honor You in private and in public alike. Amen.

23:12.devotion: God declares that the corrupt leaders' path will become slippery. Those who led others astray, walking in spiritual darkness, will stumble and fall under His judgment. This is ancient prophetic warning about divine accountability for those who abused sacred trust and misled God's people.
23:12.reflection: Am I walking in the light of God's word, or groping along a path of my own choosing?
23:12.action: Choose one decision facing you today and deliberately seek God's wisdom in Scripture before acting on it.
23:12.prayer: Father, guard my steps. Keep me from self-made paths that lead to stumbling, and anchor my walk in Your trustworthy word each day. Amen.

23:13.devotion: God observes the folly of the northern prophets who spoke in Baal's name and led Israel astray. The tragedy is twofold: their own deception, and the way they pulled others away from the living God into worship that could never save or satisfy.
23:13.reflection: Whose voices am I letting shape my view of God—and are they truly pointing me to Him?
23:13.action: Identify one influence in your life that subtly draws you from devotion to God, and take a step to limit it today.
23:13.prayer: Lord, keep me from folly. Lead me away from every voice that misleads, and fix my heart on You alone, the living God. Amen.

23:14.devotion: Jeremiah exposes something far worse in Jerusalem than in Samaria: prophets living in adultery and falsehood, even encouraging evildoers so no one repented. When leaders bless sin instead of calling for repentance, whole communities harden. God compares the corruption to Sodom and Gomorrah.
23:14.reflection: Do my words ever make wrongdoing feel acceptable instead of pointing others toward God's better way?
23:14.action: Refuse to excuse one known wrong in your life today; instead, confess it to God and take a step of genuine change.
23:14.prayer: Righteous God, deliver me from softening sin. Make me honest about my own wrongs and a truthful voice that turns people back to You. Amen.

23:15.devotion: Because profaneness spread from Jerusalem's prophets across the whole land, God announces bitter judgment—wormwood and gall, images of severe hardship and consequence. Spiritual corruption at the source poisoned everything downstream. God takes seriously the spreading influence of unfaithful teaching.
23:15.reflection: What kind of influence flows from my life into the people around me every day?
23:15.action: Speak one intentionally wholesome, faith-building word to a family member, friend, or coworker today.
23:15.prayer: Father, let what flows from me be clean and good, not bitter. Make my influence a source of life for everyone You place in my path. Amen.

23:16.devotion: God warns His people not to listen to prophets who speak visions from their own hearts. Such messages make listeners empty and worthless, offering human imagination in place of God's word. Discernment was—and remains—essential for anyone who would follow the Lord faithfully.
23:16.reflection: How can I grow in telling the difference between human opinion and God's true word?
23:16.action: Before sharing or accepting a spiritual claim today, pause and ask whether it aligns with Scripture.
23:16.prayer: Lord, give me discernment. Keep me from empty words, whether my own or others', and ground my heart in what You have actually spoken. Amen.

23:17.devotion: The false prophets offered soothing promises—peace and safety—to people who despised God and followed their own desires. It was popular religion: telling hearers what they wanted rather than what was true. Jeremiah exposes how flattery about sin leads people away from repentance and real hope.
23:17.reflection: Am I seeking comfortable affirmations, or am I willing to hear what God actually says to me?
23:17.action: Invite honest spiritual input today by asking a mature believer to tell you the truth in love about an area you avoid.
23:17.prayer: God of truth, save me from convenient lies I tell myself. Give me courage to hear Your word, even when it unsettles me, and to respond. Amen.

23:18.devotion: Jeremiah asks a piercing question: who has stood in the Lord's counsel, perceived and heard His word? The implication is that the false prophets had not. Genuine ministry flows from actually listening to God. This verse points us toward humble, attentive fellowship with God before we speak or act.
23:18.reflection: When do I actually set aside time to listen to God, rather than only talking to Him?
23:18.action: Set aside fifteen minutes today to read Scripture slowly and simply listen, asking God to speak through His word.
23:18.prayer: Lord, teach me to stand in Your counsel. Quiet my noise, open my ears to Your word, and let what I say and do flow from listening to You. Amen.

23:19.devotion: Jeremiah spoke against leaders who soothed God's people with false peace while judgment approached. This verse pictures God's coming discipline as a whirlwind—forceful and aimed at persistent wickedness. It reminds us that God takes sin seriously and will not ignore injustice forever.
23:19.reflection: Where in my life have I preferred comforting words over honest confrontation with my sin?
23:19.action: Ask God today to show you one area you have excused, and write down one honest step toward change.
23:19.prayer: Lord, do not let me settle for easy words. Search me, show me where I have wandered, and give me the courage to turn back to You today. Amen.

23:20.devotion: God's purposes would be carried out fully—His heart's intent would be accomplished, and only later would His people understand. Discipline can feel confusing in the moment, but God's plans are purposeful, and clarity often comes with time and humility.
23:20.reflection: Am I willing to trust God's purposes even when I cannot yet see what He is doing?
23:20.action: Name one confusing situation in your life and deliberately entrust it to God in a short written prayer today.
23:20.prayer: Father, Your thoughts are deeper than mine. When Your ways puzzle me, help me wait with trust rather than despair, believing You are working out what is good and right. Amen.

23:21.devotion: God plainly rejected the prophets who spoke without being sent. They ran with messages He never gave, speaking their own ideas while claiming His authority. This warns every hearer to weigh what is taught against God's actual word.
23:21.reflection: How carefully do I test what I hear, even from voices I admire?
23:21.action: Choose one teaching you heard recently and compare it with Scripture before accepting it.
23:21.prayer: Lord, guard my ears and my heart from messages that merely sound spiritual. Give me discernment to know Your voice and courage to follow it above popular opinion. Amen.

23:22.devotion: Here is what faithful ministry looks like: standing in God's counsel and speaking His words, which lead people to turn from evil. Truthful teaching produces change. God's word, faithfully delivered, calls hearers back to the right path.
23:22.reflection: When God's word convicts me, do I actually turn, or do I only listen?
23:22.action: Take one clear biblical command you know and deliberately practice it today in a specific relationship or situation.
23:22.prayer: Thank You, Lord, for Your word that tells me the truth. When I hear it, let it not stop at my ears—move my feet toward repentance and obedience today. Amen.

23:23.devotion: God is not a distant deity who cannot be reached, nor merely a familiar companion we can manage. He is both near and transcendent. This question humbles our assumptions and invites us to relate to Him as He truly is.
23:23.reflection: Do I treat God as near when I want comfort but far away when I want independence?
23:23.action: Pause once today—morning or night—and consciously acknowledge God's presence with a simple sentence of prayer.
23:23.prayer: God who is near and yet beyond all, help me live aware of You in every place and hour. Keep me from shrinking You down to fit my convenience. Amen.

23:24.devotion: No one can hide from the God who fills heaven and earth. Secret sins and hidden motives are fully visible to Him. This is sobering, yet also comforting: nothing about your life escapes the attention of a God wise enough to handle it.
23:24.reflection: What am I acting as though God cannot see?
23:24.action: Bring one hidden habit or attitude out into the open—confess it honestly to God, and if wise, to a trusted person.
23:24.prayer: Lord, You see everything about me, and You still invite me close. Thank You that nothing I hide can separate me from Your sight or Your grace. Make me honest before You today. Amen.

23:25.devotion: God heard the prophets claiming vivid dreams as His revelations. He had not spoken; the claims were fabricated. God is not indifferent to misused spiritual language—He notices when His name covers human invention.
23:25.reflection: Do I ever use religious language to make my own desires sound like God's will?
23:25.action: Before you say or share anything spiritual today, pause and check whether it is truthful or just impressive-sounding.
23:25.prayer: Father, keep my words honest. Forgive me for the times I have dressed up my own wishes in spiritual clothing. Make me a truthful voice, not a flattering one. Amen.

23:26.devotion: These prophets spoke from the deceit of their own hearts—self-deception had become their message. The condition was longstanding, and God asked how long it would continue. Hearts left unexamined can slowly make lies feel like truth.
23:26.reflection: What lie about myself or about God have I allowed to grow comfortable in my heart?
23:26.action: Spend five quiet minutes today asking God to expose one self-deception, and write down what comes to mind.
23:26.prayer: Lord, I can deceive even myself. Shine Your light into the corners of my heart, uproot the lies I have grown used to, and plant Your truth there instead. Amen.

23:27.devotion: God speaks through Jeremiah about false prophets who filled people's ears with their own dreams, steering hearts away from the Lord toward Baal. Forgetting God's name did not happen suddenly; it happened as misleading voices were trusted over God's truth, generation after generation.
23:27.reflection: Whose voices am I letting shape my heart most this week?
23:27.action: Notice one influence today that pulls your attention from God, and replace that time with reading Scripture.
23:27.prayer: Father, guard my heart from voices that make me forget You. Keep Your name first in my thoughts, and draw me back whenever I drift. In Jesus' name, amen.

23:28.devotion: Amid many competing dreams and messages, God draws a clear line: let the dreamer tell dreams, but the one who has God's word must speak it faithfully. His word is wheat, nourishing and true; mere human messages are chaff, blown away with the wind.
23:28.reflection: Do I hunger more for God's word than for easier, more entertaining messages?
23:28.action: Set aside fifteen minutes today to read Scripture carefully and take one truth to heart.
23:28.prayer: Lord, thank You for giving us Your word. Help me receive it faithfully and speak it honestly, choosing the wheat over the chaff in what I listen to and share. Amen.

23:29.devotion: God describes His word as fire and a hammer. It is not weak or decorative; it warms, purifies, and breaks through what seems immovable. Where human persuasion fails, God's word carries His own power to reach and transform stubborn hearts.
23:29.reflection: Where have I treated God's word as ordinary when it is powerful?
23:29.action: Bring one hard situation to God today, asking Him to work through His word in it.
23:29.prayer: Lord, Your word is like fire and a hammer. Break through the hard places in my heart, purify what needs cleansing, and do what my own strength cannot. Amen.

23:30.devotion: God declares He is against prophets who steal His words, taking what belongs to Him and using it for themselves. Speaking for God is a sacred trust, not a possession. Misusing His word harms neighbors who desperately need to hear it truly.
23:30.reflection: Am I careful to handle God's word honestly rather than bending it to my purposes?
23:30.action: Before sharing something spiritual today, pause and check it against Scripture first.
23:30.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have used Your words carelessly. Teach me to handle Scripture with reverence and honesty, serving others rather than myself. In Jesus' name, amen.

23:31.devotion: God opposes those who casually put words in His mouth, claiming He speaks when He has not. This warns against dressing our own opinions in divine language. To say He says when He has not spoken misleads hearers and misrepresents the holy God.
23:31.reflection: Have I ever claimed God's approval for something He never said?
23:31.action: Catch yourself today before saying God said something, and simply say, I believe, instead.
23:31.prayer: Lord, keep my tongue honest. When I speak about You, let me speak truth and humility, never claiming Your voice for my own opinions. Guard those who hear me. Amen.

23:32.devotion: God condemns those who prophesy false dreams, causing His people to err through lies and recklessness, though He never sent them. Careless spiritual teaching is not harmless; it leads real people astray. Words spoken in God's name carry weight and consequence.
23:32.reflection: Am I teaching or sharing anything spiritual carelessly, without weighing it against God's truth?
23:32.action: Choose one trusted, Bible-based teacher or resource today and test what you hear against Scripture.
23:32.prayer: Father, protect Your people from careless and false teaching, and keep me from it too. Make me careful, humble, and truthful with anything I teach or share. Amen.

23:33.devotion: When people demand an oracle from the Lord, Jeremiah is told to reply with a sobering word: God warns He will forsake them. Seeking a fresh word while refusing to obey the word already given turns even genuine seeking into presumption.
23:33.reflection: Am I asking God for new direction while ignoring what He has already told me?
23:33.action: Review one command or prompting from God you have set aside, and take one step of obedience today.
23:33.prayer: Lord, forgive me for seeking new words while neglecting old ones. Help me treasure and obey what You have already spoken before asking for more. In Jesus' name, amen.

23:34.devotion: God warns that prophets, priests, and people who carelessly claim His oracle will answer for it, with consequences reaching their households. Flippant use of divine language invites serious accountability. Speaking for God is never a light matter in His eyes.
23:34.reflection: How seriously do I take the privilege of speaking about God to others?
23:34.action: Pray briefly before your next spiritual conversation, asking God for a humble and truthful tongue.
23:34.prayer: Father, remind me that words about You carry weight. Keep me from light and careless speech, and let everything I say about You be true, reverent, and loving. Amen.

23:35.devotion: In a time when false prophets flooded Judah with their own words dressed up as divine messages, God told the people how to speak with one another: ask sincerely, What has the LORD answered? What has the LORD spoken? God wanted ordinary conversation to center on His true word, not human speculation dressed in religious language.
23:35.reflection: When I talk with other believers, do I point each other toward what God has actually said, or toward opinions and predictions?
23:35.action: In one conversation today, gently steer it toward something God has clearly said in Scripture rather than speculation or hearsay.
23:35.prayer: Lord, keep my conversations anchored in Your word. When I speak with others, help me ask what You have spoken and listen humbly for Your voice in Scripture. Amen.

23:36.devotion: God rebuked the people and prophets who tossed around the phrase the oracle of the LORD while twisting His words into whatever suited them. Treating human ideas as God's own voice, God said, perverts the words of the living God. Sacred vocabulary cannot make a false message true.
23:36.reflection: Have I ever labeled my own preferences or conclusions as though they were God's clear word?
23:36.action: Before sharing an opinion as spiritual truth today, pause and ask whether Scripture actually supports it.
23:36.prayer: Father, guard me from dressing up my own words as Yours. Give me humility to say I do not know when I do not know, and faithfulness to Your word. Amen.

23:37.devotion: God gave the people a probing question to put to every prophet who claimed to speak for Him: What has the LORD answered you? What has the LORD spoken? The question tested whether a message came from God or from the prophet's imagination. Discernment begins with asking for the source.
23:37.reflection: Do I test what I hear from teachers and voices around me by asking what God has truly spoken?
23:37.action: Choose one teaching or message you heard recently and compare it carefully with what Scripture plainly says.
23:37.prayer: Lord, make me a careful listener. Give me discernment to ask good questions of every voice claiming Your authority, and keep me rooted in Your true word. Amen.

23:38.devotion: Even after God told them to stop using the loaded phrase the oracle of the LORD, the people kept saying it, turning a sacred term into a slogan for their own messages. Their persistence in using God's language for their own purposes showed stubborn hearts that would not heed correction.
23:38.reflection: When God corrects me through His word, do I adjust, or do I keep doing the same thing in slightly new words?
23:38.action: Identify one habit God has been convicting you of, and take one honest step today to change it rather than rationalize it.
23:38.prayer: Father, forgive my stubbornness. When You correct me, let me not merely change my wording but change my heart. Make me soft and responsive to Your voice. Amen.

23:39.devotion: Because the people persisted in speaking their own words as God's words, God announced solemn judgment: He would forget, forsake, and cast them out of His presence, along with Jerusalem, the city He had given their fathers. Losing God's presence was the deepest loss of all.
23:39.reflection: Am I treasuring God's presence, or have I grown comfortable treating Him as one voice among many?
23:39.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes today simply to be with God in prayer and Scripture, valuing His presence above all else.
23:39.prayer: Lord, I do not want to live apart from Your presence. Draw near to me as I draw near to You. Make Your fellowship more precious to me than anything else. Amen.

23:40.devotion: God declared that persistent rejection of His word would bring lasting reproach and shame that would not be forgotten. This sober word describes the enduring consequence of Judah's unfaithfulness. Scripture records such warnings so that later generations, including us, would take God's word seriously.
23:40.reflection: Am I treating God's warnings as loving protection, or brushing them off as if they will never matter?
23:40.action: Thank God today for one warning in Scripture that has protected you, and share its value with someone else.
23:40.prayer: Father, thank You that Your warnings are expressions of Your care. Keep me from hardening my heart, and let Your word guard my life for Your glory. Amen.

24:1.devotion: After Babylon carried King Jeconiah, the leaders, craftsmen, and smiths into exile, God gave Jeremiah a vision of two baskets of figs placed before the temple. The setting is poignant: the symbol of fruitfulness stood before God's house while His people were experiencing the consequences of their rebellion.
24:1.reflection: When life feels like exile and loss, do I believe God still sees my situation and speaks into it?
24:1.action: Bring one painful or disorienting circumstance to God in prayer today, asking Him to help you see it through His eyes.
24:1.prayer: Lord, You see every season of my life, even exile and loss. Help me trust that You are present and at work even when circumstances feel scattered and broken. Amen.

24:2.devotion: In the vision, one basket held very good figs, ripe and ready to eat, while the other held figs so bad they were inedible. The vivid contrast prepared for God's word in the verses that follow, where He distinguishes between the exiles in two different ways. God's vision invites us to look beneath appearances to His purposes.
24:2.reflection: How might God be inviting me to look beyond surface appearances at the people and situations around me?
24:2.action: Reserve judgment today about someone whose situation looks bad on the surface, and pray for God's perspective instead.
24:2.prayer: God, You see what I cannot see. Give me humility about my own judgments and eyes to discern Your work where I would least expect it. Amen.

24:3.devotion: In a vision, God asks Jeremiah what he sees: two baskets of figs set before the temple. One holds very good figs, the other figs so rotten they cannot be eaten. Jeremiah answers honestly, describing exactly what stands before him, not yet knowing what the fruit represents.
24:3.reflection: When God asks what you see in your circumstances, do you answer honestly, even when the picture is confusing or hard?
24:3.action: Take a few minutes today to name honestly to God what you actually see in your life, without dressing it up or denying it.
24:3.prayer: Lord, You see everything about my life already. Give me courage to describe my circumstances to You honestly, trusting that You understand what I cannot yet. Amen.

24:4.devotion: After Jeremiah describes the figs, God speaks again. This brief verse reminds us that revelation unfolds in God's time and God's words. Jeremiah has seen the vision; now the meaning comes. The Lord does not leave His prophet—or His people—guessing at His purposes.
24:4.reflection: Are you waiting on God to bring understanding to something in your life you can see but do not yet comprehend?
24:4.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes today to listen for God through Scripture, asking Him to make His meaning clear in one confusing area of your life.
24:4.prayer: Speak, Lord, for Your servant is listening. When understanding tarries, help me wait patiently for Your word rather than rush to my own conclusions. Amen.

24:5.devotion: God explains the vision: the good figs represent the exiles already taken to Babylon. Surprisingly, He calls the captivity something He sent for their own good. What looked like loss was, in His hands, a means of preserving and refining His people far from Jerusalem.
24:5.reflection: Can you trust that even a painful dislocation in your life might be carrying you toward God's good purposes rather than away from them?
24:5.action: Identify one hard change or loss in your life and write one sentence asking God to use it for your good, keeping the paper where you'll see it.
24:5.prayer: Father, I don't always see Your purpose in hard seasons. Help me believe You can work for my good even where I would never have chosen to go. Amen.

24:6.devotion: God promises the exiles His attentive care: His eyes set on them for good, a future return to the land, and words of building and planting instead of tearing down. Judgment had come, but it was not the last word. Restoration is God's declared intention for the carried-away ones.
24:6.reflection: Where do you need to hear that God's plans for you are to build and plant rather than to pull down?
24:6.action: Do one small act of building today—repair something, encourage someone, or plant a seed—while thanking God that He builds what sin has broken.
24:6.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your eyes are on Your people for good. Build up the broken places in my life and in those I love, and teach me to hope again. Amen.

24:7.devotion: The deepest promise is here: God Himself will give the exiles a heart to know Him. They will be His people and He their God, and they will return to Him with their whole heart. True restoration is not merely geographic; it is spiritual, a renewed relationship God Himself creates.
24:7.reflection: Is your heart set on knowing God Himself, or only on getting your outward circumstances restored?
24:7.action: Spend five minutes today in undistracted prayer asking God for a heart that truly knows Him, and name one distraction you will set aside for that time.
24:7.prayer: God, give me a heart to know You. Draw my whole heart back to You, and let me rest in being Yours. Be my God in every season. Amen.

24:8.devotion: The bad figs, God says, represent King Zedekiah, his officials, and those who remained in Jerusalem or fled to Egypt. They resisted God's word through Jeremiah and refused the path He had set. This ancient judgment oracle shows that rejecting God's word has consequences, even for the powerful.
24:8.reflection: When God's word points you down a hard but faithful path, do you obey, or do you look for an easier escape?
24:8.action: Name one place where you have been resisting what you know God asks of you, and take the first small obedient step today.
24:8.prayer: Lord, forgive me for the times I have heard Your word and turned away. Soften my stubborn places, and make me willing to follow You even when the way is costly. Amen.

24:9.devotion: God declares that those who rejected His word will become trouble, reproach, and a byword among the nations wherever they are driven. This is hard ancient judgment language, spoken into a specific history of rebellion. It warns that a life lived against God scatters blessing rather than carrying it.
24:9.reflection: What kind of witness is your life becoming among the people around you—does it draw others toward God or away from Him?
24:9.action: Choose one relationship today where you can reflect God's grace instead of grievance, and offer a kind word or practical help there.
24:9.prayer: Father, keep my life from becoming a reproach to Your name. Let my words and ways point others to Your goodness, and heal any harm my example has caused. Amen.

24:10.devotion: The chapter closes with severe words: sword, famine, and pestilence would pursue those consumed from the land God gave their fathers. These covenant warnings describe ancient judgment on persistent rebellion. For believers today, the passage soberly reminds us that turning from God carries real loss, even as the whole chapter holds out mercy to the humble.
24:10.reflection: Is there anything in your life that persistent, unrepentant resistance to God is quietly consuming?
24:10.action: Confess one specific sin to God today and ask Him to uproot it, then share your struggle with a trusted friend or mentor for accountability.
24:10.prayer: Lord, You are holy and merciful. Do not let me drift into ruin. Root out whatever separates me from You, and keep me in the land of Your blessing. Amen.

25:1.devotion: This verse timestamps God's word: it came to Jeremiah in the fourth year of King Jehoiakim, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon. God speaks into real history, at precise moments, to a people facing upheaval. His word is not vague or timeless only; it addresses our actual circumstances and days.
25:1.reflection: Where in your real, dated life do you need to hear God's word right now?
25:1.action: Write down today's date and one specific situation you will intentionally bring before God in prayer tonight.
25:1.prayer: Lord, thank You that You speak into real history and real lives. Meet me in my actual circumstances today. Help me recognize Your word addressed to me, and give me ears ready to hear whatever You would say. Amen.

25:2.devotion: Jeremiah did not keep God's word private. He spoke it to all the people of Judah and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Faithfulness to God included courage to deliver His message publicly, even when it was unwelcome, to everyone who needed to hear it.
25:2.reflection: Is there a truth God has given you that you have been keeping to yourself instead of sharing?
25:2.action: Share one encouraging word from Scripture with a family member, friend, or coworker sometime today.
25:2.prayer: Father, make me faithful like Jeremiah, willing to speak what is true with humility and love. Keep me from hiding Your word out of fear or indifference. Use my voice today to point someone toward You. Amen.

25:3.devotion: Jeremiah recounts twenty-three years of ministry, from Josiah's thirteenth year onward. He rose early and spoke persistently, yet the people did not listen. His faithfulness is a sober picture of patient obedience: God's servants are called to speak, even when hearts remain closed.
25:3.reflection: How do you respond when you obey God faithfully but see no visible results?
25:3.action: Identify one ongoing duty you have been tempted to abandon, and faithfully carry it out again today.
25:3.prayer: Lord, strengthen me for the long obedience that does not depend on quick results. When my efforts seem fruitless, remind me that my task is faithfulness, and the outcome belongs to You. Keep me rising early to serve You. Amen.

25:4.devotion: God did not send only Jeremiah. He sent all His servants the prophets, rising early and sending them again and again. Judah's refusal was not ignorance; God had graciously and repeatedly warned them. His persistent patience stands in stark contrast to their closed ears.
25:4.reflection: How many times has God patiently sent warnings or invitations into your life, and how have you responded?
25:4.action: Recall one message or conviction God has repeated in your life, and finally act on it today.
25:4.prayer: Patient God, thank You for speaking to me again and again, even when I have not listened. Forgive my repeated delays and dull ears. Give me a heart that responds the first time You call, and keeps responding daily. Amen.

25:5.devotion: The prophets' message was simple and merciful: repent, turn from evil ways and deeds, and remain in the land God had given their fathers forever. Obedience and blessing were bound together. God's call to return was never meant to rob them, but to secure their home and heritage.
25:5.reflection: What turning away from God in your life has quietly endangered the good things He has given you?
25:5.action: Name one specific habit or behavior to repent of today, and take one step to turn from it.
25:5.prayer: Gracious Lord, thank You that Your call to repent is also a call to blessing and belonging. Turn my heart from every evil way. Help me treasure the good gifts You have given me enough to guard them with obedience. Amen.

25:6.devotion: God warned against going after other gods to serve and worship them, and against provoking Him with the works of their hands. Idolatry was not abstract; it involved real worship and human-made objects. Yet even here mercy glows: the promise, I will not harm you, shows God's desire to bless rather than punish.
25:6.reflection: What modern substitute have you been tempted to serve or worship in place of God alone?
25:6.action: Take five minutes today to name one idol in your life, then consciously release it to God in prayer.
25:6.prayer: Lord, expose anything I have set up in Your place, whether possessions, ambitions, or comforts. I do not want to provoke You with the works of my hands. Be my single worship, and keep me safely in Your care. Amen.

25:7.devotion: Judah's persistence in idolatry hurt themselves. God says they did not listen, and their rebellion with their own hands' works provoked Him to their own hurt. Sin is never a private harm; it wounds the sinner, others nearby, and the relationship with a holy and grieving God.
25:7.reflection: In what ways has your own stubbornness or disobedience caused hurt to you or those around you?
25:7.action: Consider one relationship or situation damaged by your choices, and take a first step to make amends today.
25:7.prayer: Father, forgive me for the ways my choices have hurt myself and others. I do not want to persist in what wounds me. Bring me to my senses, heal what my sin has damaged, and lead me back to Your ways. Amen.

25:8.devotion: This verse introduces consequences: because you have not heard My words. Hearing is more than listening; it is receiving and obeying. Judah's long refusal of God's gracious warnings carried real weight. The verse invites us to take seriously the difference between merely hearing and truly heeding God's voice.
25:8.reflection: What is the difference between how you listen to God's word and how you actually obey it?
25:8.action: Choose one command or invitation from Scripture you have heard but not obeyed, and obey it today.
25:8.prayer: Lord, I confess how often I hear without heeding. Do not let Your word pass over me without changing me. Make me a doer and not a hearer only, so that my life rests on what You have actually spoken. Amen.

25:9.devotion: Jeremiah speaks God's sober warning to Judah: because of persistent idolatry and injustice, judgment through Babylon is coming. Strikingly, God calls the pagan king Nebuchadnezzar 'My servant,' showing that even painful history unfolds under the LORD's sovereign hand, not by random chance.
25:9.reflection: When circumstances feel overwhelming, do I trust that God's purposes are still at work even through what I cannot control?
25:9.action: Name one situation in your life that feels out of control, and deliberately place it before God in a written prayer today.
25:9.prayer: Sovereign Lord, You rule over nations and over my circumstances. When life feels shaken, anchor my heart in Your wisdom and faithfulness. Teach me to trust You even when Your ways are hard to understand. Amen.

25:10.devotion: Judgment is described in everyday terms: wedding songs, grinding millstones, lamplight. God is warning that ordinary joys—work, celebration, home life—would be stripped away. This reminds us that common blessings are gifts, and their loss through rebellion is genuinely grievous.
25:10.reflection: Which ordinary gifts of daily life—family, work, celebration—have I been treating as guaranteed rather than received with gratitude?
25:10.action: List three ordinary blessings you enjoyed today and thank God for each one specifically, out loud or in writing.
25:10.prayer: Gracious Father, thank You for the simple gifts that fill my days: home, work, laughter, and loved ones. Forgive me for taking them for granted. Help me live today with a grateful, attentive heart. Amen.

25:11.devotion: The land would become desolate, and the nations would serve Babylon for seventy years. The judgment was real and long-lasting, yet the fixed number of years quietly pointed to God's promise that exile would not be the final word for His people.
25:11.reflection: When I face a long, difficult season, do I believe that seasons of hardship are not permanent even when they feel endless?
25:11.action: Identify someone currently enduring a prolonged trial, and send them an encouraging message or offer practical help today.
25:11.prayer: Faithful God, You know the length of every hard season I walk through. When endurance feels impossible, remind me that You set boundaries to suffering and that Your purposes never end in despair. Sustain my hope. Amen.

25:12.devotion: After seventy years, God promised to judge Babylon itself for its own iniquity. The instrument of judgment would not escape accountability. This passage teaches that God is perfectly just: no nation, power, or person escapes His righteous assessment, including those He used as instruments.
25:12.reflection: Do I trust God's justice fully enough to release my desire for payback into His hands?
25:12.action: Choose one resentment you are holding and, in prayer today, consciously hand the matter to God's justice instead of your own.
25:12.prayer: Righteous Judge, You see every wrong and will judge every injustice perfectly. Free me from bitterness and the burden of revenge. Help me trust Your justice and walk in mercy toward others as You have been merciful to me. Amen.

25:13.devotion: God declares that all He spoke through Jeremiah would certainly come to pass. His written word through the prophet was not idle talk. This underscores a comforting truth: God's word proves reliable—both His warnings and His promises can be trusted without reservation.
25:13.reflection: Am I treating Scripture as trustworthy truth that shapes my decisions, or as optional advice I consult only occasionally?
25:13.action: Read a short Bible passage slowly today and write down one concrete way it should change your attitude or behavior this week.
25:13.prayer: Lord, Your word is true and enduring. Forgive me for the times I have heard it without obeying it. Make me a doer of Your word, trusting every promise and heeding every warning You have given. Amen.

25:14.devotion: God announces that many nations and great kings would one day rule over Babylon, and that He would repay according to deeds and works. The great empire would be humbled. Power and pride offer no shelter from God's fair reckoning, whether for nations or individuals.
25:14.reflection: In what areas of life am I quietly relying on my own strength or status rather than walking humbly with God?
25:14.action: Examine one area of pride or self-reliance today, and take a practical step of humility, such as asking for help or admitting a mistake.
25:14.prayer: Almighty God, You humble the proud and repay justly. Guard my heart from arrogance and self-sufficiency. Teach me to walk humbly before You, doing works of faith and love that honor You rather than myself. Amen.

25:15.devotion: God gave Jeremiah a dramatic prophetic picture: a wine cup of fury to be carried to the nations. The imagery symbolized God's approaching judgment on many peoples. It is sobering language portraying God's holiness confronting widespread sin—not a model for human vengeance.
25:15.reflection: How seriously do I take God's holiness, and am I honest about my own need for His mercy rather than His judgment?
25:15.action: Spend five quiet minutes today in honest self-examination before God, confessing specific sins and thanking Him for mercy offered through Christ.
25:15.prayer: Holy God, the thought of Your judgment makes me sober. I do not stand above anyone, but only by Your mercy. Cleanse my heart, keep me from pride, and make me a messenger of Your grace to others. Amen.

25:16.devotion: The nations who drank from the cup would stagger and go mad under the sword God sent. The picture conveys the overwhelming disorientation of coming judgment. Yet for God's people, this chapter ultimately calls for repentance—turning back to the LORD before pride brings ruin.
25:16.reflection: Is there any area where I am drifting from God, hoping consequences will simply never arrive?
25:16.action: Identify one habit or choice you know needs to change, and take the first practical step to turn from it today.
25:16.prayer: Merciful Lord, You warn us because You love us and do not delight in judgment. Show me where my heart is drifting. Give me courage to repent today, and draw me back into close fellowship with You. Amen.

25:17.devotion: Jeremiah faithfully obeyed a hard commission: he took the cup of God's judgment from the Lord's hand and made every nation the Lord sent him to drink from it. The prophet did not enjoy delivering this message, but he obeyed. Sometimes faithfulness means speaking truth that is unwelcome, trusting that God's word is right even when it is heavy.
25:17.reflection: Am I willing to obey God even when the task He gives me is difficult or unpopular?
25:17.action: Identify one truth God has placed on your heart that you have been avoiding sharing, and take one humble step toward addressing it today.
25:17.prayer: Faithful Lord, give me courage like Jeremiah's. When Your word is hard to speak or hear, help me to obey You anyway, trusting Your wisdom above my comfort. Strengthen me for the tasks You assign. In Jesus' name, amen.

25:18.devotion: The cup began with Jerusalem and Judah. God's own people, with their kings and princes, faced the desolation that Jeremiah had long warned them about. Judgment starts with the household of God because privilege brings responsibility. The verse stands as a sober reminder that being called by God's name is never a license to ignore His voice.
25:18.reflection: Do I take God's call on my life seriously, or do I assume His patience means His warnings can be ignored?
25:18.action: Prayerfully review one area of your life where you have grown complacent about obedience, and write down one specific change you will make.
25:18.prayer: Holy God, search my heart. Forgive me for the times I have taken Your grace lightly. Let me never mistake Your patience for indifference to sin. Draw me back to wholehearted obedience today. In Jesus' name, amen.

25:19.devotion: Pharaoh, Egypt's powerful king, was next in the list. Egypt had seemed an unshakable ally and a refuge for Judah's leaders, yet even its king, servants, princes, and people stood under the same cup. Earthly power and alliances cannot shield anyone from God's righteous standards. What looks mighty to us is small before the Lord of all nations.
25:19.reflection: Where am I tempted to place my trust in human strength, wealth, or alliances rather than in God alone?
25:19.action: Name one worldly security you lean on, and deliberately spend time today leaning on God instead through prayer or Scripture.
25:19.prayer: Almighty God, forgive me for the times I have trusted what is visible instead of You. You alone are my refuge and strength. Teach me to rely on Your power, not the fading securities of this world. In Jesus' name, amen.

25:20.devotion: The cup reached the mixed multitudes, the kings of Uz, and the Philistine cities of Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and Ashdod. Israel's long-standing neighbors and rivals were not exempt. God's authority extends over every people group and border, not just one nation. His justice is universal, and no community, however distant or different, lives outside His sight.
25:20.reflection: Do I remember that God cares about all peoples, even those I find foreign, distant, or difficult to love?
25:20.action: Pray today by name for one nation or people group different from your own, asking God's mercy and justice for them.
25:20.prayer: Lord of all nations, Your eyes are on every people and every land. Broaden my heart to care for those beyond my own circle. May Your justice and mercy reach everywhere, and use me as You will. In Jesus' name, amen.

25:21.devotion: Edom, Moab, and Ammon, Israel's close relatives and frequent adversaries, also drank from the cup. These nations descended from kin of Israel, yet shared history did not excuse their ways. God judges each people by His own righteous standard. The nearness of our background or relationships cannot substitute for a life that honors Him.
25:21.reflection: Does my familiarity with God's things actually shape the way I live, or has it become only a background I rely on?
25:21.action: Choose one habit of obedience you know God asks of you and practice it deliberately today, letting familiarity become faithfulness.
25:21.prayer: Gracious Father, do not let me rest on heritage, church background, or knowledge about You. Make my faith living and active. Help me walk in genuine obedience that honors You each day. In Jesus' name, amen.

25:22.devotion: The cup passed to Tyre and Sidon, wealthy trading cities, and to the kings of the distant coastlands across the sea. Commerce, riches, and sea-lanes of influence could not shield them. God's word reached even the far horizons of the ancient world. His sovereign claim extends past every boundary of wealth, geography, and human achievement.
25:22.reflection: Am I living as if God's authority reaches into my finances, work, and ambitions, not just my Sunday life?
25:22.action: Bring one specific area of your finances or work before God today and ask Him to guide how you use it.
25:22.prayer: Sovereign Lord, every sea and shore belongs to You, and so does every corner of my life. Rule over my work, my money, and my plans. May nothing I pursue sit outside Your lordship. In Jesus' name, amen.

25:23.devotion: Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who dwelt in the farthest corners came under the cup as well. Even remote desert peoples, seemingly forgotten at the edge of the map, were within God's knowledge and purpose. No one is too hidden or too far away to be known by the Lord. His gaze reaches every distant place.
25:23.reflection: Do I believe God sees and knows me even in the hidden, unnoticed corners of my life?
25:23.action: Bring one hidden struggle or private part of your life honestly before God in prayer today, trusting He already knows and cares.
25:23.prayer: Lord, You see every far corner of the world and every far corner of my heart. Nothing about me is hidden from You. Help me live honestly before You, trusting Your kind and knowing eyes. In Jesus' name, amen.

25:24.devotion: The kings of Arabia and the desert's mixed multitudes completed the wide sweep of the cup. Nomadic peoples who moved beyond settled borders still stood accountable to the Lord of all the earth. Wandering or settled, powerful or obscure, every nation answered to Him. God's righteous authority spans the whole earth and every kind of people in it.
25:24.reflection: Am I living today in awareness that God's rightful authority covers every place and every moment of my life?
25:24.action: Before you go to bed tonight, review your day with God and surrender any area where you resisted His ways.
25:24.prayer: Lord of the whole earth, every land and every people answers to You, and so do I. Keep me mindful of Your reign in every place I go today. Make my life an offering to You. In Jesus' name, amen.

25:25.devotion: In this list of nations destined to face God's judgment, Jeremiah names Zimri, Elam, and the Medes. The catalogue underscores that no power, however distant or obscure, stands outside God's awareness. He sees every kingdom, every ruler, and every deed done in the wide world He governs.
25:25.reflection: Where in my life have I acted as if God does not see or care about what happens far from me?
25:25.action: Pray today for one nation or people far from you, asking God's mercy and justice to be known there.
25:25.prayer: Lord of all nations, You see every corner of the earth and every ruler upon it. Teach me to trust Your sovereign view of the world, and let me pray faithfully for peoples I will never meet. Amen.

25:26.devotion: Jeremiah's roll call expands to every king near and far, until all the kingdoms of the earth are included, ending with Sheshach, understood as a code name for Babylon. Even the mightiest empire will not escape the cup of judgment God holds. Human power has limits before Him.
25:26.reflection: Which powers or systems in my world do I silently assume are beyond God's authority?
25:26.action: Write down one current power or institution, then pray over it, affirming God's authority above it.
25:26.prayer: Father, no kingdom outranks You, and no empire escapes Your justice. Keep me from fearing human power more than Your word, and anchor my hope in Your unshakable throne. Amen.

25:27.devotion: God instructs Jeremiah to command the nations to drink from the cup of His wrath, a vivid picture of judgment they cannot refuse or withstand. The imagery is harsh, reminding readers that turning from God carries real consequences. Scripture presents judgment soberly, not gleefully.
25:27.reflection: How do I respond when I encounter difficult passages about God's judgment rather than skipping past them?
25:27.action: Read a judgment passage slowly today and jot one honest thought about God's justice in your journal.
25:27.prayer: Holy God, Your justice is real, and Your word does not hide it. Give me honesty to face hard passages, reverence for Your righteousness, and gratitude for the mercy You offer through repentance. Amen.

25:28.devotion: When the nations refuse the cup, God declares they will certainly drink. There is no negotiation, no escape, and no exemption once His judgment is determined. The verse confronts us with the seriousness of resisting God and the futility of defying His settled word.
25:28.reflection: Am I currently resisting a conviction from God that I have been trying to negotiate away?
25:28.action: Name one area of resistance in prayer today, and choose one small step of obedience you can take now.
25:28.prayer: Lord, forgive me for the times I resist Your voice and bargain with Your convictions. Soften my heart to obey You promptly, trusting that Your ways lead to life even when they are hard. Amen.

25:29.devotion: God announces that judgment begins with Jerusalem, the city called by His name. If His own people do not escape accountability, the nations certainly will not. Judgment starts at the household of God, a principle echoed later in the New Testament, calling God's people to humility rather than presumption.
25:29.reflection: Do I hold others to God's standards more readily than I hold myself?
25:29.action: Before correcting anyone today, examine yourself honestly in prayer and address your own shortcoming first.
25:29.prayer: Father, You are impartial, and being called by Your name is a weighty gift, not a shield. Search my heart first, purify Your people, and keep me from presumption and pride. Amen.

25:30.devotion: Jeremiah is told to proclaim God's word against all nations, pictured as a roar from heaven like a lion defending His fold, and a shout like harvest treaders singing. The passage portrays God rising publicly to speak against evil, not silently watching it spread.
25:30.reflection: When I see evil flourish in the world, do I believe God will ultimately speak and act, or does it breed quiet despair?
25:30.action: When you encounter news of injustice today, respond with a brief prayer entrusting it to God's justice.
25:30.prayer: God who roars from on high, You are not indifferent to evil or silent about injustice. Help me trust Your righteous voice above the noise of the world and wait on You with steady hope. Amen.

25:31.devotion: God has a controversy, a legal dispute, with the nations, and He will plead His case against all flesh. The courtroom imagery shows judgment flowing from reasoned divine justice, not random anger. The wicked face the sword because their deeds deserve it, while God's verdicts are always just.
25:31.reflection: If God brought a case against my life today, what would the evidence reveal about my choices?
25:31.action: Invite God to examine you today, then confess one specific wrong you have put off acknowledging.
25:31.prayer: Righteous Judge, You see every deed and weigh every motive. Bring Your case to my own heart now, mercifully, so I may repent and walk honestly with You before that final day. Amen.

25:32.devotion: God warns that disaster will move from nation to nation like a gathering whirlwind, sweeping in from the farthest corners of the earth. Trouble in this broken world is not aimless; God remains sovereign even over upheaval. His people can trust Him amid storms they cannot control.
25:32.reflection: When turmoil spreads through the world, where do I instinctively place my security?
25:32.action: Identify one anxiety about world events, then surrender it to God in a written prayer today.
25:32.prayer: Lord of hosts, whirlwinds of trouble move through this world, yet nothing escapes Your hand. Steady my heart when nations shake, and anchor my security in You alone, my unmovable refuge. Amen.

25:33.devotion: Jeremiah's prophecy describes judgment sweeping across the nations, so widespread that normal mourning and burial become impossible. In ancient Near Eastern culture, burial honored the dead; its absence signaled utter devastation. The passage reminds us that God's justice is real, and rebellion against Him carries consequences no one can escape or soften.
25:33.reflection: When I consider God's holiness and judgment, does it stir me toward humility and repentance rather than indifference?
25:33.action: Take five minutes today to silently examine your heart, naming one attitude or habit you've excused, and confess it honestly to God.
25:33.prayer: Holy God, Your justice is perfect even when it is sobering to read. Keep me from casual rebellion, and draw me into honest repentance. Root my hope in Your mercy, and teach me to walk humbly with You today. Amen.

25:34.devotion: Here judgment falls first on the shepherds—the kings, priests, and leaders responsible for God's people. Those entrusted with care of others are called to wail in ashes, falling like shattered precious vessels. Scripture consistently holds leaders to account, because mishandling God's flock wounds real people entrusted to their watch.
25:34.reflection: Where has God given me responsibility for others—family, workplace, church—and am I tending that trust faithfully?
25:34.action: Identify one person whose wellbeing you influence, and do one deliberate act of care or encouragement for them today.
25:34.prayer: Lord, You see how I lead and influence those You've placed near me. Forgive where I have been careless with the trust You gave. Make me a shepherd after Your own heart—patient, honest, and protective of those in my care. Amen.

25:35.devotion: This verse declares that the shepherds and leaders will find no escape. Privilege and position cannot shield anyone from God's righteous judgment. It is a sobering word: human power, wealth, or influence offers no refuge when we stand before the Lord who sees every heart and every deed.
25:35.reflection: Am I quietly trusting something in this world—status, money, connections—to protect me from what only God's mercy can cover?
25:35.action: Name one earthly security you lean on more than God, and take a practical step today to loosen its grip, such as simplifying or giving.
25:35.prayer: Father, forgive me for the shelters I build apart from You. You alone are my refuge, and no position or possession can take Your place. Help me trust You plainly today and rest in the mercy You offer through Christ. Amen.

25:36.devotion: The wailing of leaders is heard by the flock, for the LORD has plundered their pasture. What was entrusted for nourishing the people is taken away. The verse shows how failed leadership brings loss that ripples outward—when shepherds fall, the sheep feel it. Faithful stewardship matters to God and to everyone under it.
25:36.reflection: When my choices affect the people around me, do I consider how my faithfulness or failure touches their lives too?
25:36.action: Choose one way your decisions impact others—speech, habits, or reliability—and make one concrete improvement in it today.
25:36.prayer: Lord of the flock, thank You for caring deeply about how we treat one another. Guard me from self-serving choices that wound others. Give me wisdom in my responsibilities, and let my life nourish the people You've placed around me. Amen.

25:37.devotion: The peaceful dwellings are cut down because of the LORD's fierce anger against persistent, unrepentant sin. Jeremiah speaks into a nation that had long ignored prophetic warning. This ancient judgment narrative reminds us that God is not indifferent to rebellion, while pointing us to seek His mercy while it may be found.
25:37.reflection: Is there a warning God has been gently repeating to me that I keep postponing rather than obeying?
25:37.action: Recall one repeated nudge from God—about a relationship, habit, or commitment—and act on it today instead of delaying again.
25:37.prayer: Patient God, You warn us because You love us, not because You delight in judgment. Soften my heart to Your repeated invitations. Give me courage to obey today what I have postponed, and keep me tender toward Your voice. Amen.

25:38.devotion: God is pictured as a lion leaving His lair, and the land becomes desolate under fierce judgment. Jeremiah's imagery conveys that the Lord is not a passive observer; He actively responds to injustice and oppression. This was spoken as prophecy over nations of Jeremiah's day, calling hearers to sober reverence before Him.
25:38.reflection: Do I treat God as a distant figure, when Scripture shows He is present, aware, and engaged with how people live?
25:38.action: Spend a few minutes today acknowledging God's real presence in an ordinary moment—before a meeting, a meal, or a hard conversation.
25:38.prayer: Lord, You are not distant from our world or our daily lives. Wake me from treating You casually. Let reverence for Your holiness shape my choices, and draw me near through the mercy You so freely extend. Amen.

26:1.devotion: This verse dates Jeremiah's next message to the beginning of King Jehoiakim's reign. The timestamp matters: a new ruler on the throne did not mean a new word from heaven. God's message continued unchanged through political transitions, reminding us that His truth does not shift with human governments or seasons.
26:1.reflection: Do I let changing circumstances—news, leadership, uncertainty—quiet the voice of God in my life?
26:1.action: Anchor your day in something unchanging: read a short Scripture passage this morning before checking your phone or the news.
26:1.prayer: Unchanging God, the world around me shifts quickly, but Your word stands. Keep me steady when circumstances change and headlines unsettle me. Anchor my hope not in earthly powers but in You, whose faithfulness outlasts every reign. Amen.

26:2.devotion: God commands Jeremiah to stand in the temple court and speak to worshipers from all Judah, without diminishing a word. Jeremiah must deliver God's message completely, however unwelcome it may be. This charge honors the fullness of God's word and calls every messenger of truth to faithfulness over popularity or personal safety.
26:2.reflection: Am I ever tempted to soften, trim, or skip what God says because it might cost me approval?
26:2.action: Choose one truth from Scripture you've been hesitant to live or share, and act on it plainly and graciously today.
26:2.prayer: Faithful God, You spoke to Jeremiah whole and true, and You call me to the same honesty. Remove my fear of others' opinions. Let me receive Your word fully, live it visibly, and speak it gently without trimming its edge. Amen.

26:3.devotion: God sends Jeremiah to preach at the temple gate, and His words reveal His heart: the warning itself is an invitation. Judgment was threatened because of persistent evil, yet God holds out the possibility of mercy if the people will listen and turn. Even His severest warnings carry a redemptive purpose, showing that God desires repentance and restoration rather than destruction.
26:3.reflection: When God convicts me of something wrong in my life, do I hear it as condemnation or as a loving invitation to turn back to Him?
26:3.action: Identify one habit or attitude God has been nudging you about, and take one intentional step today to turn from it.
26:3.prayer: Merciful Father, thank You that Your warnings are acts of grace, calling me home. Give me a soft heart that listens quickly and turns to You without delay. Amen.

26:4.devotion: Jeremiah's message begins with a clear condition: listening to the Lord means walking in His law. God had graciously set His instruction before His people, and obedience was the expected response. This verse reminds us that hearing God's word is never meant to end with hearing; genuine listening is demonstrated in daily, practical faithfulness to what He has spoken.
26:4.reflection: Is there a difference right now between what I hear from God and how I actually live?
26:4.action: Choose one clear biblical instruction you already know and practice it deliberately today, letting obedience follow your hearing.
26:4.prayer: Lord, I confess that hearing is easier than obeying. Help me walk in Your ways today, not merely nod at Your word. Make my life match what I profess. Amen.

26:5.devotion: God had patiently sent prophet after prophet, rising early to send them, yet the people refused to heed them. This verse shows both God's persistent patience and the people's stubborn resistance. He did not leave them without guidance or warning; He continually pursued them through messengers. Their failure was not a lack of revelation but a refusal to respond.
26:5.reflection: What voices has God placed in my life to speak truth to me, and am I truly heeding them?
26:5.action: Reach out today to a mentor, pastor, or mature friend and ask them to speak honestly into one area of your life.
26:5.prayer: Patient God, thank You for persistently speaking to me through Your word and through faithful people. Forgive me for times I have tuned out truth. Give me ears that heed Your messengers. Amen.

26:6.devotion: God warns that persistent disobedience will bring devastating consequences: the temple would become like Shiloh, a former sanctuary site that had been abandoned, and the city would become a cautionary word among the nations. This was not casual threatspeak but a solemn reminder that privileges long abused can be lost. Even the sacred is not exempt from the consequences of continued rebellion.
26:6.reflection: Am I treating any blessing or privilege from God as something I can take for granted forever?
26:6.action: Write down three blessings you may have been treating as automatic, and thank God for each one specifically today.
26:6.prayer: Holy God, keep me from presuming upon Your grace. Help me treasure what You have given rather than assume it will always be there. Cultivate reverence and gratitude in my heart. Amen.

26:7.devotion: Jeremiah delivered the message publicly in the temple, and the priests, prophets, and all the people heard it. The warning was given openly, in the very place of worship, so no one could claim ignorance. This verse reminds us that God's word often confronts us in unexpected settings, and hearing it places responsibility on us to respond rather than dismiss.
26:7.reflection: When God's word confronts me in a sermon, conversation, or Scripture reading, what do I usually do with it?
26:7.action: After your next time in Scripture or a sermon, write one sentence about what you heard and one step you will take in response.
26:7.prayer: Lord, You speak to me in ordinary places and moments. Keep me from shrugging off what I hear. Let every encounter with Your word move me toward response and change. Amen.

26:8.devotion: As soon as Jeremiah finished speaking, the religious leaders and the crowd seized him and declared he must die. Faithful proclamation of an unpopular message met immediate hostility. This verse shows the real cost that can come with speaking God's truth, and it distinguishes ancient events from how we respond today: we are called to faithfulness even when truth is unwelcome, trusting God with the results.
26:8.reflection: Have I ever stayed silent about something God calls true because I feared how people would react?
26:8.action: Speak one truth graciously today where it would be easier to stay quiet, doing so with kindness and respect.
26:8.prayer: Father, give me courage to be faithful when truth is unpopular. Guard my words from harshness, but keep me from cowardly silence. Help me trust You with the consequences. Amen.

26:9.devotion: The crowd confronted Jeremiah, quoting his own words back at him and gathering against him in the temple. Notice their outrage focused on the message's content rather than any search for whether it was true. This verse warns against measuring a message by how it makes us feel. When God's word unsettles us, the right response is examination, not outrage.
26:9.reflection: When a message stings me, do I pause to ask whether it is true, or do I simply get defensive?
26:9.action: Next time a teaching or conversation pricks your conscience, pray before reacting, and ask God to show you any truth you need to face.
26:9.prayer: Lord, forgive me for the times I have shot the messenger because the message hurt. Give me humility to examine my heart first, and grace to receive hard truths well. Amen.

26:10.devotion: When word reached the officials of Judah, they left the king's house and came to the temple, sitting at the New Gate to hear the matter. In the midst of a hostile mob, a channel of due process opened. God often provides means of justice and advocacy in tense situations, and this verse reminds us to value fair, orderly processes rather than mob reactions.
26:10.reflection: When conflict or accusation arises around me, do I seek to understand fairly, or do I join the loudest voices?
26:10.action: If you are involved in a disagreement today, listen to both sides fully before forming or voicing a judgment.
26:10.prayer: God of justice, thank You that You care about fair processes and honest hearing. Make me slow to condemn and quick to listen, especially when tensions run high. Guide those who lead with wisdom. Amen.

26:11.devotion: Jeremiah has just delivered a hard word of judgment at the temple, and the reaction is swift. The priests and prophets seize him, declaring before the officials and crowd that he deserves death for speaking against the city. It is a tense moment when God's messenger stands accused simply for delivering the message he was given.
26:11.reflection: When a difficult truth confronts me, is my first response defensiveness or a willingness to listen?
26:11.action: Today, when someone offers criticism that stings, pause before reacting and honestly ask whether there is truth in it.
26:11.prayer: Lord, soften my heart when Your truth challenges me. Keep me from silencing voices You have sent, and give me humility to hear hard words with an open spirit. In Jesus' name, amen.
