33:20.prayer: Creator God, the rising and setting of the sun testifies that You keep Your covenants. Teach me to trust Your steady faithfulness in ordinary days, and anchor my hope in Your unchanging word. Amen.

33:21.devotion: God argues from the greater to the lesser: only if day and night could cease might His covenant with David fail. He promises a son on David's throne and continued priestly ministry. For Christians, this points to Christ, the promised descendant who reigns forever.
33:21.reflection: Where am I doubting a promise of God that His own faithfulness in creation contradicts?
33:21.action: Write down one biblical promise you struggle to believe, and place it somewhere visible today as a reminder of God's reliability.
33:21.prayer: Faithful Lord, just as day follows night, Your promises stand firm. Thank You for keeping Your covenant with David, fulfilled in Jesus, our reigning King. Help me trust Your word when circumstances whisper otherwise. Amen.

33:22.devotion: God pledges to multiply David's descendants and the ministering Levites beyond counting, like the stars and the sand. What looked like a dying royal line and priesthood would flourish by God's power. His promise exceeds human measurement and defies the despair of the moment.
33:22.reflection: Do I measure God's promises by my circumstances instead of by His unlimited power?
33:22.action: Spend five minutes tonight looking at the night sky or recalling it, and praise God that His promises are beyond counting.
33:22.prayer: Lord of endless promise, Your commitments to Your people outnumber the stars. Forgive my small expectations. Widen my vision to trust You for more than I can measure, and rest in Your abundant faithfulness. Amen.

33:23.devotion: Once again the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah. The repetition reassures a besieged people that God had not finished speaking. He continued to address the doubts swirling among them, meeting fear and confusion with fresh, personal communication from heaven.
33:23.reflection: When doubts swirl around me, do I bring them to God's word or let them harden into despair?
33:23.action: Name one doubt or fear you are carrying, write it down, and bring it explicitly to God in prayer before evening.
33:23.prayer: Speaking God, thank You that You keep addressing my fears with Your word. Meet me again today where doubt gathers, and replace despair with fresh confidence in Your ongoing, personal care. In Jesus' name, amen.

33:24.devotion: People were saying the Lord had cast off the two families He chose, implying His people would cease to be a nation. God takes this talk seriously, for it despised both His people and His promise. He refuses to let despairing voices define His covenant commitment.
33:24.reflection: Whose discouraging voices am I allowing to speak louder than God's promises about His people and me?
33:24.action: Replace one despairing or cynical comment today with an encouraging word about God's faithfulness to someone you talk to.
33:24.prayer: Lord, guard my heart and my speech from despairing words that contradict Your promises. When others speak as though You have given up, help me hold fast to Your covenant love and speak hope instead. Amen.

33:25.devotion: God begins His answer to the doubters by citing His appointed ordinances of heaven and earth. The fixed order of creation undergirds His argument: He who governs day and night can surely govern Israel's future. His covenant reliability is as settled as the cosmos itself.
33:25.reflection: Do I trust the God who ordered the heavens to also order the details of my life?
33:25.action: Thank God in prayer for three specific things in your life that reflect His orderly, trustworthy care.
33:25.prayer: God of order, You appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth, and nothing escapes Your governance. Teach me to trust You with my future as surely as I trust You to hold the universe together. Amen.

33:26.devotion: At the end of God's promise to restore Israel, He anchors His mercy in His covenant with Jacob, David, and Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. God declares that He will not cast away their descendants but will bring back their captives and show them mercy. Even after judgment, His covenant faithfulness stands firm.
33:26.reflection: Where have I doubted God's faithfulness to His promises when circumstances looked hopeless?
33:26.action: Write down one promise of God you cling to today and thank Him aloud for keeping His word.
33:26.prayer: Faithful God, thank You that Your mercy does not fail even when we have wandered far. Restore what has been lost, and anchor my hope in Your unbreakable covenant love through Jesus Christ. Amen.

34:1.devotion: Jeremiah receives a word from the LORD at a moment of national crisis: Nebuchadnezzar's army, with allied kingdoms, is attacking Jerusalem and the surrounding cities. This verse sets the scene for God's message to Judah's last king, showing that God still speaks clearly even when judgment has arrived.
34:1.reflection: Am I listening for God's word even in the hardest seasons of my life, not only when things go well?
34:1.action: Spend five quiet minutes today inviting God to speak to you through Scripture amid your current pressures.
34:1.prayer: Lord, in seasons of pressure and fear, help me turn to Your word rather than panic. Speak plainly to my heart, and give me ears to hear You when circumstances feel overwhelming. Amen.

34:2.devotion: God sends Jeremiah to King Zedekiah with an unwelcome message: Jerusalem will fall into Nebuchadnezzar's hand and be burned with fire. Jeremiah's faithful preaching shows that obedience to God sometimes means delivering truth people do not want to hear, even when the consequences are sobering.
34:2.reflection: Do I welcome God's truth when it confronts me, or only when it comforts me?
34:2.action: Ask one trusted person today whether there is any truth you have been avoiding, and listen without arguing.
34:2.prayer: Lord, give me courage like Jeremiah to receive Your truth honestly, even when it is hard. Keep me from softening Your word to suit my comfort, and lead me to repentance and hope. Amen.

34:3.devotion: God tells Zedekiah that he cannot escape the Babylonians. He will be captured, brought face to face with Nebuchadnezzar, and taken to Babylon. The passage is a sober reminder that we cannot outrun the consequences of persistent disobedience, though God continues to speak even then.
34:3.reflection: What consequence am I hoping to escape rather than facing honestly before God?
34:3.action: Name one situation you have been running from, and take one practical step today to face it with God's help.
34:3.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have tried to evade what I must face. Help me walk honestly before You, trusting that even in consequences I cannot escape, Your presence goes with me. Amen.

34:4.devotion: Even within judgment, God speaks a word of mercy to Zedekiah: he will not die by the sword. The chapter shows that God's justice is precise and His mercy real; discipline does not mean total abandonment. God's word holds both the hard truth and a measure of grace.
34:4.reflection: Have I mistaken God's discipline for His rejection, forgetting that He still cares for those He corrects?
34:4.action: Thank God today in a short prayer for His mercy you have received even inside a difficult correction or trial.
34:4.prayer: Gracious God, thank You that even Your discipline carries mercy. When I face the results of my choices, help me trust that You have not cast me off, but still speak peace to me. Amen.

34:5.devotion: God promises Zedekiah that he will die in peace, honored with the burial customs given former kings, with lament and incense. God declares He has pronounced this word. It is a striking picture of God's faithfulness: He keeps even hard promises exactly, and His word can be trusted fully.
34:5.reflection: Do I trust that God's word is reliable even when I only understand part of what He is doing?
34:5.action: Recall a time God carried you through a hard season, and share that memory with someone today or write it down.
34:5.prayer: Faithful Lord, Your word stands when everything else falls. Teach me to trust every promise You have spoken, resting in the assurance that You finish what You declare. Steady my heart in You. Amen.

34:6.devotion: Jeremiah faithfully delivers all these words to Zedekiah in Jerusalem itself, in the very city under siege. Obedience meant standing in the danger zone to speak God's message. This verse quietly honors the prophet's courage in speaking the whole counsel of God where it was needed most.
34:6.reflection: Is there a place of fear where God is calling me to speak or act faithfully anyway?
34:6.action: Do one small faithful thing today that fear has kept you from doing, such as an honest conversation or witness.
34:6.prayer: Lord, give me courage to obey You right where I am, even when it feels unsafe or unpopular. Help me speak and live Your truth faithfully, trusting You with the results. Amen.

34:7.devotion: As Jeremiah spoke, the Babylonian army pressed Jerusalem, Lachish, and Azekah, the last fortified cities of Judah left standing. The message of God arrived while the walls were still being tested. Even at the brink of collapse, God was still reaching out to His people with His word.
34:7.reflection: Am I open to God's voice now, while there is still time to respond, rather than waiting until things fall apart?
34:7.action: Identify one area of disobedience you have delayed addressing, and begin turning from it today with a concrete step.
34:7.prayer: Patient God, thank You that You keep speaking to me even when I have waited too long. Give me a responsive heart today, so that I turn to You while You may be found. Amen.

34:8.devotion: Jerusalem was under siege, and King Zedekiah made a covenant with the people to proclaim liberty to their slaves. This word came to Jeremiah in that tense moment, when the nation reached for obedience to God's law even as their world was falling apart.
34:8.reflection: When pressure mounts in my life, do I turn toward God's ways or away from them?
34:8.action: Identify one commitment to God you have been postponing, and take one concrete step toward it today.
34:8.prayer: Lord, in seasons of fear and crisis, help me turn to You rather than away from You. Make me quick to obey Your word, even when circumstances feel overwhelming. In Jesus' name, amen.

34:9.devotion: The covenant called each person to release Hebrew slaves, refusing to hold a fellow countryman in bondage. God's law had long required such freedom, and this verse captures the community agreeing to honor the dignity and liberty of their own brothers and sisters.
34:9.reflection: Am I treating the people closest to me with the dignity God says they deserve?
34:9.action: Consider someone whose freedom or wellbeing you may restrict by selfish demands, and deliberately lighten that burden today.
34:9.prayer: Father, open my eyes to anyone I have held too tightly, whether by unfair expectations or control. Teach me to honor every person as Your image-bearer. Grant me a generous and releasing heart. Amen.

34:10.devotion: The princes and people heard the terms of the covenant and obeyed, releasing their slaves. For a moment, Jerusalem did what was right. Obedience began well, showing that even a struggling community can respond to God's word with real, visible action.
34:10.reflection: When God's word confronts me, do I respond with prompt obedience or delay?
34:10.action: Complete one act of obedience you have been putting off, doing it today without further delay.
34:10.prayer: Lord, give me the kind of heart that hears Your word and acts on it promptly. Thank You for moments when obedience feels joyful. Keep me faithful beyond first impressions. In Christ's name, amen.

34:11.devotion: Soon afterward, the people reversed course, dragging back the freed slaves into bondage. Their repentance evaporated once the emergency pressure eased. This sober verse shows how quickly good intentions can collapse when obedience becomes costly or inconvenient.
34:11.reflection: Have I ever taken back a commitment to God once it stopped being convenient?
34:11.action: Write down one promise you made to God, and set a reminder to keep it faithfully this week.
34:11.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times my obedience has been temporary or self-serving. Anchor my commitments in Your grace, not in passing emotion. Help me finish what I begin with You. In Jesus' name, amen.

34:12.devotion: God did not stay silent when His people broke their covenant. He sent His word again through Jeremiah. Even in judgment narratives like this, God's continued speaking reveals His patience; He confronts sin because He has not given up on His people.
34:12.reflection: How do I respond when God's word confronts something I would rather ignore?
34:12.action: Spend ten minutes in Scripture today, inviting God to point out anything in your life He wants to address.
34:12.prayer: Thank You, Lord, that You speak to me even when I have failed You. Give me soft ears and a humble heart to receive Your correction as love, not condemnation. In Jesus' name, amen.

34:13.devotion: God reminded Israel that He brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, and bound Himself to them by covenant. Because they had been freed by God, He called them to reflect that deliverance in how they treated others.
34:13.reflection: How should remembering what God has rescued me from change the way I treat people?
34:13.action: Recall a specific way God has freed or healed you, and share that memory with someone today.
34:13.prayer: Lord, You brought me out of my own places of bondage through Jesus. Let gratitude for my deliverance shape my dealings with others. May I never forget what You have done for me. Amen.

34:14.devotion: God recalled His ancient command: after six years of service, a Hebrew brother was to be set free. Yet He acknowledged that their fathers never obeyed nor inclined their ear. Disobedience, He shows, had become a generational habit that this generation repeated.
34:14.reflection: What pattern of ignoring God's voice might I be repeating rather than breaking?
34:14.action: Name one way of disregarding God's instruction you learned or practiced long ago, and intentionally choose obedience instead today.
34:14.prayer: Father, break any inherited or long-practiced habit of ignoring Your voice in my life. Help me incline my ear and obey, so that my generation honors You better than the last. In Jesus' name, amen.

34:15.devotion: God acknowledged that the people had recently turned and done what was right, proclaiming liberty to their neighbors and making a covenant in His house. He notices genuine obedience, even when it is later undone. His words here carry both commendation and the weight of what follows.
34:15.reflection: Is my obedience to God a lasting posture, or only a moment I can point back to?
34:15.action: Choose one right thing you once did for God or others, and restart it today as a lasting habit.
34:15.prayer: Lord, You see every time I have turned and done right. Help my obedience be a lifestyle, not a memory. Keep me faithful in Your house and before Your name. In Jesus' name, amen.

34:16.devotion: During the Babylonian siege, Judah's leaders made a covenant to free their Hebrew slaves, honoring God's law. But when danger temporarily lifted, they reversed course and re-enslaved them. God names this as profaning His name, because promises made in His name reflect on His character.
34:16.reflection: Have I ever kept a promise to God only while circumstances made it convenient?
34:16.action: Review one commitment you made to God or others, and take a concrete step today to honor it fully.
34:16.prayer: Father, keep my word trustworthy. Where I have honored You only when it cost me nothing, give me grace to follow through, even when keeping promises becomes inconvenient or costly. Amen.

34:17.devotion: Because the people proclaimed liberty but then revoked it, God announces a solemn irony: He will proclaim liberty to them, but to the sword, pestilence, and famine. This is a prophetic judgment word from an ancient covenant context, not a pattern for how God deals with His people today.
34:17.reflection: What does it reveal about God that He takes broken promises to others this seriously?
34:17.action: Choose one person you have wronged or shortchanged, and begin making it right today, however small the first step.
34:17.prayer: Lord, You see how I treat the vulnerable around me. Forgive me where my actions contradict my words. Make me someone who brings real freedom and fairness to others, not just in speech. Amen.

34:18.devotion: Covenants in the ancient world were sometimes sealed by cutting an animal in two and passing between the halves, symbolizing solemn commitment. Judah's leaders had performed this rite before God and then broke their word. Jeremiah confronts the gravity of vows made publicly before the Lord.
34:18.reflection: When I make commitments before God, do I treat them as binding or as optional aspirations?
34:18.action: Write down one covenant-like commitment you have made, and schedule time this week to follow through on it.
34:18.prayer: God of covenant, You are faithful to every word You speak. Teach me to speak with the same integrity. When I promise before You and others, let my yes be yes, backed by obedient action. Amen.

34:19.devotion: The judgment names every class of covenant participant: princes, officials, priests, and common people. All had passed between the calf's parts and all had broken the agreement. Before God, status and position offered no exemption from accountability for injustice done to the enslaved.
34:19.reflection: Do I excuse myself from obedience because of my position, wealth, or role?
34:19.action: Identify someone over whom you hold some power, and do one intentional act today that serves their good rather than your own.
34:19.prayer: Lord, no rank or reputation shields me from Your sight. Help me use whatever influence I have to protect others, not to advantage myself. Make me faithful in the small authority You have given me. Amen.

34:20.devotion: Jeremiah pronounces severe consequences on those who broke the covenant and exploited the people they had freed. This is an ancient judgment oracle describing historical consequences, not a model for how believers should treat anyone. Its enduring lesson is that God defends the enslaved and takes covenant breaking seriously.
34:20.reflection: How does knowing God defends the oppressed change the way I see my own choices?
34:20.action: Support one person facing exploitation or hardship today, through practical help, advocacy, or giving to a trustworthy ministry.
34:20.prayer: Father, You hear the cries of those held down by others. Keep me from any action that profits from someone else's bondage, and give me courage to stand with those who suffer injustice. Amen.

34:21.devotion: King Zedekiah, who participated in the broken covenant, is named specifically along with his princes. The Babylonian army, which had briefly withdrawn, would return. Personal and national decisions carried real historical consequences, and even a king could not outrun the accountability of God's word.
34:21.reflection: Where am I hoping circumstances will hide the gap between my promises and my practice?
34:21.action: Confess one specific inconsistency to God today, and tell one trusted person who can help you stay accountable.
34:21.prayer: Lord, You see every part of my life, including what I keep quiet. Deliver me from the illusion that time or distraction will erase my failures. Grant me honest repentance and a fresh start today. Amen.

34:22.devotion: The chapter closes with God's declaration that the Babylonians would return, and Judah's cities would become desolate. This was fulfilled in history as covenant unfaithfulness ran its course. Even in severe judgment, Scripture shows God warning beforehand, giving people opportunity to turn and obey.
34:22.reflection: What is God patiently warning me about right now that I keep postponing?
34:22.action: Take one concrete step today toward obedience you have been delaying, no matter how small it feels.
34:22.prayer: Patient God, thank You that You warn and wait before consequences fall. Do not let me mistake Your patience for indifference. Wake my heart today to obey You promptly and fully. Amen.

35:1.devotion: This verse introduces a new episode: during the reign of Jehoiakim, Jeremiah received another word from the Lord. The timing shows that God continued speaking to His people through the prophet across different kings and crises. Even in a nation's decline, God's voice kept coming, offering truth and opportunity to respond.
35:1.reflection: Am I listening for God's word in hard seasons, or only when life feels stable?
35:1.action: Set aside fifteen quiet minutes today to read Scripture and listen, asking God what He is saying to you now.
35:1.prayer: Lord, You keep speaking even when everything around us is shaking. Quiet my heart to hear You today. Give me a soft, responsive spirit, so that Your word finds obedience and not resistance in me. Amen.

35:2.devotion: God sends Jeremiah on an unusual errand: invite the Rechabites into a temple chamber and offer them wine. This is no trap but a test God is setting up to expose the contrast between a family faithful to an earthly father's instructions and Judah's stubborn refusal to heed their heavenly Father's voice.
35:2.reflection: When God asks something uncomfortable of me, do I respond with obedience or with excuses?
35:2.action: Complete one small task God has already placed on your heart today, even if it feels inconvenient or unusual.
35:2.prayer: Faithful Father, help me trust You even when Your instructions seem strange. Give me a willing heart that responds promptly to Your voice, and let my obedience today draw me closer to You. In Jesus' name, amen.

35:3.devotion: Jeremiah personally gathers Jaazaniah, his relatives, and the entire household of the Rechabites. The scene is deliberate and public. God is bringing this faithful nomadic family into view, preparing them to become a living witness before all of Judah through their quiet consistency.
35:3.reflection: Who in my life models quiet faithfulness that I could learn from right now?
35:3.action: Identify one person whose steady faithfulness inspires you, and thank them for their example today.
35:3.prayer: Lord, thank You for the faithful people You place in my life as examples. Open my eyes to their quiet obedience, and help me learn from their consistency rather than overlooking them. In Jesus' name, amen.

35:4.devotion: Jeremiah brings the Rechabites into a specific chamber belonging to Hanan, described as a man of God, located near the princes' quarters. The setting within the temple adds weight to the coming test, placing this simple family among respected spaces as their faithfulness is about to be displayed.
35:4.reflection: Does my faith remain steady when I am placed in unfamiliar or intimidating settings?
35:4.action: Hold to one of your convictions today even in a setting where it would be easier to compromise.
35:4.prayer: God of Hanan, a man of God, make me faithful in every room I enter. Whether among the influential or the ordinary, let my convictions stand firm because they rest on You. In Jesus' name, amen.

35:5.devotion: Jeremiah sets bowls full of wine and cups before the Rechabites and invites them to drink. The test is straightforward and tempting. Everything is arranged so their obedience will be genuinely tested, not merely assumed, revealing whether their commitment holds under real pressure.
35:5.reflection: What does my response to temptation reveal about what I truly value?
35:5.action: Notice today where you face a small temptation, and choose the faithful response instead of the easy one.
35:5.prayer: Father, You test hearts not to fail us but to reveal what we love. Strengthen me when temptation comes, and let my choices show that my devotion to You is real. In Jesus' name, amen.

35:6.devotion: The Rechabites simply refuse: they will drink no wine, because their ancestor Jonadab commanded it. Their reply is respectful, unhesitating, and grounded in a family tradition of obedience. In the next verses God will hold this up as a stunning contrast to Judah's disobedience to Him.
35:6.reflection: If I obeyed God the way these people honored their ancestor, what would my life look like?
35:6.action: Choose one clear biblical instruction you know well, and practice it consistently throughout the rest of today.
35:6.prayer: Lord, these words challenge me. Forgive me for treating Your commands as negotiable. Give me the Rechabites' readiness to obey without argument, so that honoring You becomes my settled way of life. In Jesus' name, amen.

35:7.devotion: Jonadab's instructions shaped an entire way of life: no houses, no crops, no vineyards, only tents, so the family might live as sojourners in the land. This was a human family covenant, not a universal command for all believers, yet it illustrates how wholehearted, generational commitment shapes daily choices.
35:7.reflection: What daily habits and priorities show where my true security lies?
35:7.action: Examine one habit today that reflects attachment to comfort more than trust in God, and adjust it.
35:7.prayer: Father, I confess how much my comfort shapes me. Teach me to hold this world loosely, like a sojourner, and to find my security in You alone rather than in what I build or own. In Jesus' name, amen.

35:8.devotion: The Rechabites declare that they have obeyed Jonadab in everything he charged them, including their wives, sons, and daughters. Their obedience was comprehensive, inclusive of the whole household, and sustained across generations. It stands as a living rebuke to Judah, who had not obeyed God even once in the same way.
35:8.reflection: Does my obedience reach every area of my life, or only the convenient parts?
35:8.action: Pick one area of your life you have kept off-limits to God, and surrender it to Him in prayer today.
35:8.prayer: Lord of every generation, I want my whole household and whole life marked by obedience to You. Show me the corners I have withheld, and help me yield them completely today. In Jesus' name, amen.

35:9.devotion: The Rechabites summarize their obedience: no houses built, no vineyards, fields, or seed. Every detail of their conduct matched their commitments. Their consistency over time, amid changing circumstances, is precisely what God will use in the following verses to shame and challenge unfaithful Judah.
35:9.reflection: Am I the same person in private as I claim to be in public?
35:9.action: Review your commitments to God at day's end tonight, and honestly note where your conduct has matched them.
35:9.prayer: Faithful God, You see every detail of my days. Make my life consistent, my private conduct matching my public testimony, so my obedience to You endures through every season. In Jesus' name, amen.

35:10.devotion: The Rechabites explain their way of life to Jeremiah: they have lived in tents and kept every command of their ancestor Jonadab. For generations they honored a family commitment, showing how faithfully passing on convictions can shape a community across time.
35:10.reflection: What godly commitments from my upbringing have I kept, and which have quietly slipped away?
35:10.action: Name one faithful practice you received from family or mentors and deliberately carry it out today.
35:10.prayer: Father, thank You for the faithful examples You have placed in my life. Help me treasure and continue the good patterns I have been given, and keep my heart steady in obedience to You. Amen.

35:11.devotion: Even the obedient Rechabites adapted when war came, fleeing into Jerusalem for safety. Faithfulness does not require rigidity in every circumstance; they kept the heart of their father's command while responding wisely to real danger around them.
35:11.reflection: Where might God be asking me to hold fast to what matters while adapting wisely to changed circumstances?
35:11.action: Identify one situation where fear is pressing you, and respond today with wisdom rather than abandoning your convictions.
35:11.prayer: Lord, when danger and uncertainty press in, give me wisdom to act prudently without letting fear override my faithfulness to You. Anchor my heart in what does not change. Amen.

35:12.devotion: With the Rechabites' testimony before him, Jeremiah receives a fresh word from the LORD. God often uses the faithfulness of ordinary people to spotlight what He wants to say to His own covenant community.
35:12.reflection: Am I paying attention when God speaks through the example of someone else's faithfulness?
35:12.action: Think of one believer whose obedience challenges you, and ask God what He is saying to you through them.
35:12.prayer: Lord, open my ears to hear You however You choose to speak—through Scripture, through people, through circumstances. Don't let me miss Your voice today. Make me attentive and responsive. Amen.

35:13.devotion: God asks a piercing question: will Judah not receive instruction and obey His words? The comparison is pointed—people who ignored God's prophets were being shamed by a family that faithfully obeyed a human father for generations.
35:13.reflection: Is there instruction God has given me that I am still refusing to receive?
35:13.action: Write down one thing you know God has asked of you, and take the first obedient step today.
35:13.prayer: Father, You know the places where I have hardened my heart. Soften me to receive Your instruction. I don't want to be someone who hears but does not obey. Teach me, Lord. Amen.

35:14.devotion: God contrasts Jonadab's descendants, who obeyed a human command for generations, with Judah, who ignored God's repeated, patient warnings. His long-suffering persistence—rising early and speaking—met with persistent refusal from His own people.
35:14.reflection: How have I responded to God's patient, repeated warnings in my life—with obedience or indifference?
35:14.action: Recall a conviction God has repeated to you over time, and finally act on it today.
35:14.prayer: Lord, You have been so patient with me, speaking again and again. Forgive me for treating Your persistence as background noise rather than loving care. Give me a responsive, obedient heart. Amen.

35:15.devotion: God sent prophet after prophet calling Judah to turn from evil, amend their ways, and abandon other gods—with a promise of continued dwelling in the land. Obedience was not demanded without hope; grace and warning traveled together, and still they would not listen.
35:15.reflection: When God calls me to turn from something, do I hear only the demand, or also His kindness?
35:15.action: Take a walk or quiet moment today to ask God honestly: is there an evil way You want me to turn from right now?
35:15.prayer: Father, thank You that Your call to repentance always comes with mercy. Help me see Your warnings as invitations to life, not burdens. Turn my heart fully toward You today. Amen.

35:16.devotion: The contrast reaches its sharpest point: the sons of Jonadab performed their father's commandment, while God's own people would not obey Him. Faithfulness to a lesser, human authority exposed the emptiness of Judah's excuses for ignoring the greater One.
35:16.reflection: Do I show more consistency toward human commitments than toward my commitment to God?
35:16.action: Examine your promises today—to people and to God—and take one step to make right the one you've neglected.
35:16.prayer: Lord, expose the inconsistency in my life with kindness, not condemnation. I want to be as faithful to You as I am to the people and obligations I respect. Make my obedience whole. Amen.

35:17.devotion: After generations of speaking and calling, God declares judgment: because He spoke and they did not hear, called and they did not answer, the doom He pronounced would come. Persistent refusal of God's voice carries real consequences, even for His covenant people.
35:17.reflection: If God has been calling and I have not answered, what has my silence been costing me?
35:17.action: Set aside ten minutes today to sit quietly before God and answer the call you've been putting off.
35:17.prayer: Father, I don't want to be someone You call and I never answer. Forgive my delayed responses. Give me ears that hear today, and a heart that answers promptly and gladly. Amen.

35:18.devotion: The Rechabites had faithfully obeyed their ancestor Jonadab's instructions, even when Jeremiah tested them by offering wine. God pointed to their obedience as a contrast to Judah's stubborn refusal to listen to Him. Their faithfulness to a human father's word becomes a living sermon about honoring God's word.
35:18.reflection: When someone I trust gives me wise guidance, do I follow it as readily as the Rechabites followed theirs?
35:18.action: Follow through today on one commitment you have already made but been putting off.
35:18.prayer: Lord, thank You for people whose example of faithfulness challenges me. Help me obey Your word not just briefly but consistently, honoring You with steady, willing trust in my daily choices. Amen.

35:19.devotion: Because the Rechabites honored their father's commands, God promised that a descendant of Jonadab would always stand before Him. This blessing shows that God notices quiet, faithful obedience. While the nation around them wavered, this family's constancy was remembered and rewarded by the Lord.
35:19.reflection: Does my everyday faithfulness reflect a trust in God who sees and remembers it?
35:19.action: Do one unseen act of obedience today without seeking recognition or telling anyone about it.
35:19.prayer: Father, You see the faithfulness no one else notices. Keep me steady when culture shifts around me. Let my life and my household stand before You, generation after generation, faithful to Your word. Amen.

36:1.devotion: In the fourth year of King Jehoiakim, God gave Jeremiah a new assignment. After years of speaking prophetic messages, Jeremiah was now directed to preserve them in writing. God was making sure His word would endure in a form people could hear, read, and remember even after Jeremiah himself was gone.
36:1.reflection: How am I treating God's word—as something passing, or as something worth treasuring and preserving in my life?
36:1.action: Write out or journal one Scripture verse today so you can return to it later.
36:1.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your word is enduring and not fleeting. Help me treat Scripture as precious, storing it in my heart and returning to it often, so it shapes my life for years to come. Amen.

36:2.devotion: God commanded Jeremiah to record on a scroll all the words he had prophesied since the days of Josiah—warnings for Israel, Judah, and the nations. Nothing was to be left out. God wanted the complete message available, because partial truth would not fully serve the people who needed to hear it all.
36:2.reflection: Do I listen to all of God's word, including the parts that challenge me?
36:2.action: Spend ten minutes today reading a Bible passage you usually avoid or find uncomfortable.
36:2.prayer: Father, forgive me when I prefer only the comforting parts of Scripture. Give me courage and humility to hear Your whole word, trusting that even Your hard truths are spoken in love for my good. Amen.

36:3.devotion: The purpose of the scroll was mercy, not merely warning. God hoped that when Judah heard of the coming adversity, everyone would turn from evil—and then He would forgive their iniquity and sin. Even in judgment's shadow, God's heart was open to repentant people, ready to pardon.
36:3.reflection: Is there a wrong direction in my life that God has been gently calling me to turn from?
36:3.action: Name one specific sin or habit to God today in prayer, and take one practical step away from it.
36:3.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your warnings are invitations, not dead ends. You long to forgive. Give me a soft heart that turns quickly to You, and receive me with the mercy You promise. Amen.

36:4.devotion: Jeremiah dictated, and Baruch the son of Neriah wrote the words on a scroll. Jeremiah could not do this work alone; God provided a willing assistant. The word of the Lord reached the people through faithful cooperation—both the prophet's speaking and the scribe's careful writing were part of God's plan.
36:4.reflection: Am I willing to serve God in supporting roles, or do I only want tasks that make me visible?
36:4.action: Offer practical help today to someone in your church or family carrying a heavy responsibility.
36:4.prayer: Father, thank You for the quiet servants like Baruch whose faithful work carries Your word forward. Show me where I can serve behind the scenes, and make me dependable in whatever task You give. Amen.

36:5.devotion: Jeremiah explained to Baruch that he was confined and could not go to the temple himself. Restricted from the public task, he still found a way for God's word to be proclaimed. Baruch would go in his place. Physical limitation did not silence the message God wanted His people to hear.
36:5.reflection: When circumstances limit what I can do, do I look for the ways God's purpose can still move forward through me?
36:5.action: If something is limiting you today, take one small step anyway—encourage someone by call, message, or prayer.
36:5.prayer: Lord, when my circumstances confine me, remind me that Your purposes are not bound. Show me the way open to me, however small it seems, and use it to carry Your word to others. Amen.

36:6.devotion: Jeremiah instructed Baruch to read the scroll publicly in the temple on a day of fasting, when crowds from all over Judah would gather. The timing was strategic: people assembled, humbled, and attentive would hear God's word together. God's message was meant for ears beyond Jeremiah's immediate circle.
36:6.reflection: Whom in my life needs to hear God's word, and am I willing to share it with them?
36:6.action: Share one verse or word of encouragement from Scripture with someone today, in person or by message.
36:6.prayer: Father, Your word is meant to be heard, not hidden. Give me courage to share Scripture with the people around me, and prepare their hearts to listen, turn, and find Your forgiveness. Amen.

36:7.devotion: Jeremiah was confined and could not go to the temple himself, so God's word through him was written on a scroll for Baruch to read aloud publicly. The hope behind this mission was repentance: that hearing God's warning, the people would cry out to the Lord and turn from their evil ways, even with judgment already pronounced.
36:7.reflection: When God's word confronts me, do I respond with softness and repentance or with hardened indifference?
36:7.action: Choose one habit or attitude you know grieves God, and take a concrete step today to turn from it, such as apologizing or seeking accountability.
36:7.prayer: Lord, let Your word not bounce off my heart. Give me ears that hear and a will that turns. When I am convicted, lead me quickly to repentance and prayer, trusting Your mercy. In Jesus' name, amen.

36:8.devotion: Baruch faithfully carried out everything Jeremiah commanded. He read God's words from the scroll in the temple, taking on a risky public role during a season of national rebellion. His quiet obedience made the proclamation possible, showing how God works through willing servants who deliver His word faithfully.
36:8.reflection: Am I willing to do unglamorous, even risky, obedience when God asks something difficult of me?
36:8.action: Complete one task today you believe God has placed before you, even if it feels small, unnoticed, or uncomfortable for you.
36:8.prayer: Father, thank You for faithful people like Baruch who carried Your word to others. Make me dependable in small and hard assignments alike. Help me value obedience over comfort, and serve You quietly and courageously. In Jesus' name, amen.

36:9.devotion: In the ninth month of Jehoiakim's fifth year, a fast was proclaimed in Jerusalem for all the people, including visitors from Judah's towns. Gathered for fasting and solemn assembly, the crowd was uniquely prepared to hear God's word read aloud, since fasting often marked a seeking of the Lord in crisis.
36:9.reflection: When I gather with God's people, am I truly prepared to hear from Him, or is my heart distracted and distant?
36:9.action: Set aside thirty minutes today to fast from something meaningful to you and use that time to listen to Scripture.
36:9.prayer: Lord, You gather Your people to hear Your voice. Prepare my heart before I open Scripture or join worship. In seasons of trouble, teach me to seek You sincerely through prayer and fasting, not merely through outward routine. Amen.

36:10.devotion: Baruch read the scroll from a chamber near the New Gate of the temple, in the hearing of all the people. God's word was proclaimed openly, not hidden. The public setting meant ordinary worshipers, not just officials, heard the warnings and promises that Jeremiah had written down years earlier.
36:10.reflection: Do I give God's word the same public, unhurried attention in my life that these listeners gave it that day?
36:10.action: Read Scripture aloud today, either alone or with family or friends, letting your ears as well as your eyes receive God's word.
36:10.prayer: Gracious God, thank You that Your word is meant to be heard openly, not kept private or safe. Give me a listening heart when Scripture is read, and boldness to share it respectfully with others. In Jesus' name, amen.

36:11.devotion: Michaiah, grandson of the scribe Shaphan, heard the reading and took it seriously. Rather than dismissing it or keeping it to himself, he recognized the words came from the Lord and mattered urgently. One attentive listener became the link that carried the message to Judah's leaders.
36:11.reflection: When I hear God's word, do I treat it as life-changing news worth carrying to others, or as mere background noise?
36:11.action: Share one verse or truth from Scripture with a friend, family member, or coworker today in a natural, respectful conversation.
36:11.prayer: Lord, make me like Michaiah—alert, receptive, and ready to act on what I hear from You. Deliver me from spiritual dullness. Use my simple faithfulness to carry Your word to people who have not yet heard it. Amen.

36:12.devotion: Michaiah went down to the scribe's chamber in the king's house, where the princes of Judah were sitting together. This was the seat of government influence. God's word, heard at the temple, was now moving toward the highest levels of national leadership, through the report of one attentive hearer.
36:12.reflection: Do I believe God's word is relevant enough to bring into the influential places and conversations of my world?
36:12.action: Identify one setting where you tend to keep faith silent, and look for a gracious way to speak of God there this week.
36:12.prayer: Father, Your word belongs in every room, from temples to council chambers. Give me courage and wisdom to speak of You where decisions are made and opinions are strong. Let Your truth be heard among the influential. In Jesus' name, amen.

36:13.devotion: Michaiah declared to the princes all the words he had heard Baruch read. He reported faithfully and completely, not editing or softening the message. His accuracy mattered, because these leaders would soon weigh the scroll's words themselves. Faithful transmission of God's word required honesty, courage, and careful memory.
36:13.reflection: When I repeat what God has said in Scripture, do I communicate it faithfully, or do I trim its hard edges?
36:13.action: Before sharing a Bible passage with someone today, read it carefully first so you represent it accurately rather than loosely.
36:13.prayer: Lord, guard me from distorting Your word, whether by softening it or using it carelessly. Give me diligence to know it well and integrity to pass it on truthfully, trusting Your Spirit to make it clear. Amen.

36:14.devotion: The princes sent Jehudi to summon Baruch and his scroll, and Baruch came to them. The officials wanted to hear the words directly rather than rely on a secondhand report. Baruch's willingness to appear before authorities shows steady courage rooted in confidence that God's word deserved a hearing.
36:14.reflection: If asked to stand and explain God's word before skeptical or powerful people, would I come willingly or shrink back?
36:14.action: Practice explaining the hope you have in Christ in two or three simple sentences, so you are ready if the opportunity arises today.
36:14.prayer: Father, when opportunities come to speak Your word before those who may question or oppose it, give me Baruch's steadiness. Let me come willingly, speak humbly, and trust You with the results. Strengthen me by Your Spirit. In Jesus' name, amen.

36:15.devotion: Jeremiah had been barred from the temple, so he dictated God's words to Baruch, who read them publicly. When officials heard about the scroll, they asked Baruch to read it to them privately. Even powerful men paused to listen before acting, showing that God's word deserves a hearing before judgment or decision.
36:15.reflection: When was the last time I gave God's word a genuinely open hearing before forming my opinion?
36:15.action: Choose one Bible passage today and read it slowly twice, resisting the urge to rush past it.
36:15.prayer: Lord, give me a listening heart. Slow me down long enough to hear Your word before I react, decide, or speak. Amen.

36:16.devotion: After hearing the scroll's warnings of judgment, the officials looked at one another in fear. Unlike the king who would later dismiss the message, these men took God's warning seriously. Holy fear is the right response when Scripture confronts us with truth we would rather avoid.
36:16.reflection: Do I treat God's warnings as serious words meant for me, or as curiosities I can shrug off?
36:16.action: Identify one warning or conviction from Scripture you have been ignoring, and write it where you will see it today.
36:16.prayer: Father, grant me reverent fear instead of careless indifference. Let Your warnings soften my heart rather than harden it. Amen.

36:17.devotion: The officials carefully asked how the scroll came to be written. They wanted to know whether these words truly came from Jeremiah at God's direction. Their questions remind us that weighing the source and reliability of a message matters, especially when a message demands a response.
36:17.reflection: When I hear teaching that claims to come from God, do I take care to test where it really came from?
36:17.action: Before sharing or believing one spiritual claim today, pause and check it against Scripture itself.
36:17.prayer: Lord, give me discernment. Help me weigh every message carefully and cling to what is truly from You. Amen.

36:18.devotion: Baruch testified plainly: Jeremiah spoke the words aloud, and Baruch wrote them with ink in a book. There was nothing mysterious about the process—God's message came through ordinary, faithful human obedience. Scripture itself came to us through such humble, careful work of hearing and recording.
36:18.reflection: Am I willing to serve God in unglamorous tasks, like writing, copying, or carrying a message that isn't mine?
36:18.action: Offer practical help today to someone whose ministry or work goes largely unnoticed.
36:18.prayer: Thank You, Lord, for faithful, ordinary servants through whom Your word has traveled to me. Make me willing to serve quietly too. Amen.

36:19.devotion: Concerned for their safety, the princes told Baruch and Jeremiah to go and hide, for the king would likely reject the scroll's message. Sometimes faithfulness to God's word requires prudence and even withdrawal from danger. Trusting God and taking wise precautions are not opposites.
36:19.reflection: Is there a situation in my life where wisdom calls for caution rather than confrontation right now?
36:19.action: Take one prudent step today to protect your health, safety, or integrity, trusting God while acting wisely.
36:19.prayer: Father, give me both courage and wisdom. Show me when to speak openly and when to step back, trusting You either way. Amen.

36:20.devotion: The officials left the scroll safely stored in Elishama's chamber and reported the words to the king in the court. They preserved the message even as they carried it upward. God's word was treated as something precious to be guarded, not discarded once it had been heard.
36:20.reflection: How carefully do I handle God's word—do I guard it in my heart or set it aside after hearing it?
36:20.action: Memorize one verse today, storing God's word where no one can take it from you.
36:20.prayer: Lord, help me treasure Your word, keeping it safe in my heart and carrying it faithfully to others. Amen.

36:21.devotion: King Jehoiakim sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll from Elishama's chamber, and it was read aloud before the king and his princes. The moment of decision had arrived: would the king humble himself under God's word or reject it? Every hearer of Scripture eventually faces that same fork in the road.
36:21.reflection: When God's word confronts me, do I move toward obedience or toward excuses?
36:21.action: Pick one command of Scripture you have been delaying, and take the first obedient step today.
36:21.prayer: Lord, when Your word comes to me, keep me from delay and defiance. Give me the grace to obey promptly and gladly. Amen.

36:22.devotion: The scene shifts quietly to the king sitting in his winter house, a fire burning on the hearth before him. It is a cozy picture that will soon turn grim, for this warmth will be used against the scroll itself. Comfort can dull us to the urgency of God's word.
36:22.reflection: Has my comfort or routine made me numb to what God has been trying to say to me?
36:22.action: Step out of your comfort zone once today to listen to someone God may be using to speak to you.
36:22.prayer: Father, don't let comfort make me complacent. Wake my heart to Your voice, even when it disturbs my warmth and ease. Amen.

36:23.devotion: Jeremiah's words from the Lord were written on a scroll and read aloud to King Jehoiakim. As the warning of judgment was read column by column, the king took a knife, cut the scroll apart, and burned it piece by piece, attempting to destroy God's message rather than respond to it with humility.
36:23.reflection: When God's word confronts something in my life, do I respond with openness, or do I quietly try to silence it?
36:23.action: Choose one Scripture that convicts you and, instead of avoiding it, read it slowly today and write down what it asks of you.
36:23.prayer: Lord, keep me from the hard-heartedness of King Jehoiakim. When Your word cuts against my comfort, give me a soft heart that listens, repents, and obeys rather than resists Your truth. Amen.

36:24.devotion: After the king burned the scroll, neither he nor his servants showed any fear or remorse, even though they had heard the Lord's warning in full. In ancient Israel, tearing garments signified grief and repentance, but no such response came. Their refusal to tremble at God's word revealed hearts already hardened against correction.
36:24.reflection: Has familiarity with God's word dulled my sense of awe and my willingness to be corrected by it?
36:24.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes today to read Scripture aloud and ask God to restore your reverence for His voice.
36:24.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have heard Your word without trembling. Awaken my heart to take Your warnings and promises seriously, and let reverence for You shape my daily choices. Amen.

36:25.devotion: Not everyone in the court joined the king's defiance. Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah pleaded with Jehoiakim not to burn the scroll, honoring God's word even when it was unpopular. Their courage was costly and, humanly speaking, unsuccessful, yet Scripture records their faithfulness as a quiet witness against the king's rebellion.
36:25.reflection: When those around me dismiss or resist God's truth, am I willing to speak up, even if it changes nothing immediately?
36:25.action: Identify one place today, at work, home, or online, where you can respectfully stand for biblical truth or defend someone being wronged.
36:25.prayer: Lord, give me the quiet courage of Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah. Help me speak for what is right even when I stand alone or seem to fail, trusting You with the results. Amen.

36:26.devotion: Enraged, King Jehoiakim ordered the arrest of Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. Yet the Lord hid them from the king's men. This brief verse shows God's protective care over His messengers. Though they faced real danger for faithfully proclaiming God's word, the Lord shielded them according to His purposes.
36:26.reflection: Do I trust God to be my refuge when faithfulness to Him brings risk, criticism, or opposition?
36:26.action: Pray today for Christians facing real danger or persecution for their faith, asking God to shelter and strengthen them.
36:26.prayer: Gracious God, thank You that You watch over those who serve You. Protect and strengthen believers who face danger for proclaiming Your word, and give me that same trust in Your care. Amen.

36:27.devotion: The king's fire consumed the scroll, but it could not silence the Lord. After the burning, the word of the Lord came again to Jeremiah. God was not defeated by human defiance; He remained active, speaking, and sovereign. The destruction of the scroll became the occasion for an even greater word to follow.
36:27.reflection: Do I believe that no human power, rejection, or hostility can ever nullify or destroy the word of the living God?
36:27.action: Memorize a short verse today that reminds you God's word endures, and recall it whenever you feel discouraged about the state of the world.
36:27.prayer: Eternal God, thank You that Your word cannot be burned, silenced, or overturned. When it seems the world rejects Your truth, remind me that You are still speaking and still sovereign. Amen.

36:28.devotion: God commanded Jeremiah to take a new scroll and rewrite every word the king had burned. This divine command shows God's commitment to His message and His patience in giving Judah another chance to hear it. What human pride destroyed, God restored completely, adding further words of judgment against the defiant king.
36:28.reflection: Where in my life have I tried to push away God's word, and is He graciously bringing it back to me now?
36:28.action: Return today to one portion of the Bible you have long avoided, and read it prayerfully, asking God to help you receive it.
36:28.prayer: Patient Lord, thank You for refusing to give up on those who reject You. Thank You that Your word returns to us with grace. Help me welcome it this time with an obedient heart. Amen.

36:29.devotion: God sent a pointed message to Jehoiakim, naming his specific act of rebellion: burning the scroll that warned of Babylon's invasion. God confronted the king directly, showing that defiance of His word does not go unnoticed. Judgment was not arbitrary; it answered the king's own contempt for the Lord's gracious warning.
36:29.reflection: Am I honest with myself about the specific ways I have resisted God, or do I hide behind generalities?
36:29.action: In prayer today, name one specific area of disobedience before God, confess it plainly, and ask Him for grace to change.
36:29.prayer: Search me, O God, and show me the specific places where I have resisted You. Give me honesty to confess and grace to turn, trusting in Your mercy through Christ. Amen.

36:30.devotion: Because Jehoiakim rejected God's word, the Lord announced consequences: his dynasty would lose the throne, and his body would be denied an honorable burial, exposed to heat by day and frost by night. The passage records God's judgment on a defiant king, reminding us that rejecting God's word carries real and sobering consequences.
36:30.reflection: If I continue treating God's warnings as optional, what consequences am I inviting into my own life and legacy?
36:30.action: Write down one warning or invitation from Scripture you have been delaying, and take the first obedient step toward it today.
36:30.prayer: Righteous Lord, Your judgments are just and true. Save me from complacency toward Your word. Grant me a heart that hears Your warnings as mercy and responds today, not tomorrow. Amen.

36:31.devotion: King Jehoiakim had burned the scroll containing God's word, refusing to repent when he heard it. Here the Lord declares that his rejection carries consequences, not only for him but for those who followed his lead. God's warning, ignored, does not disappear; judgment falls on a nation that would not listen.
36:31.reflection: When God's word confronts me, do I humble myself, or do I find ways to silence it?
36:31.action: Identify one command or warning from Scripture you have been avoiding, and take one honest step of obedience toward it today.
36:31.prayer: Father, give me a soft heart toward Your word. Keep me from the pride that cuts up and burns what convicts me. Help me listen, repent, and obey, trusting Your wisdom above my own. In Jesus' name, Amen.

36:32.devotion: After the king burned the first scroll, God's word was not destroyed. Jeremiah dictated the message again to Baruch, and this time even more words were added. Burning a book could not burn away God's truth. His word endures beyond every attempt to suppress it.
36:32.reflection: Am I confident that God's word stands firm, even when culture, power, or my own fears push against it?
36:32.action: Spend time today reading Scripture instead of only hearing about it, and thank God that His word cannot be silenced.
36:32.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your word survives every fire and every attempt to bury it. Give me courage like Jeremiah and Baruch, who rewrote what was destroyed. Anchor my life in Your enduring truth. Through Christ, Amen.

37:1.devotion: This verse marks a change of kings. Zedekiah, son of good King Josiah, now rules Judah, installed by Babylon after the exile of his nephew Coniah. A new ruler sat on the throne, but the nation's underlying problem, rebellion against God's word, remained unchanged.
37:1.reflection: Do I expect new circumstances or new leaders to fix what only a changed heart before God can fix?
37:1.action: Name one situation you have hoped would resolve itself externally, and ask God to begin His work in your own heart first.
37:1.prayer: Gracious God, You remain sovereign through every change of leadership and season. Stop me from pinning hope on circumstances rather than on You. Renew my heart so that change begins where it truly matters. In Jesus' name, Amen.

37:2.devotion: Zedekiah, his officials, and the ordinary people of the land all alike refused to heed the words the Lord spoke through Jeremiah. The rejection was not one man's failure but a shared, whole-society turning away from God, even while disaster warnings grew louder.
37:2.reflection: Am I listening to God's word for myself, or drifting along with the indifference of the people around me?
37:2.action: Choose one way to stand with God's word today even if friends or coworkers shrug at it, and do it quietly and graciously.
37:2.prayer: Lord, forgive me for the times I have drifted with the crowd away from Your voice. Give me ears that heed You and courage that does not depend on company. Keep me faithful when others will not listen. Amen.

37:3.devotion: Strikingly, Zedekiah sent officials to ask Jeremiah to pray for them. He would not obey God's word, yet he wanted God's help in crisis. Prayer without obedience is a fragile refuge; the king sought intercession while rejecting the very message the prophet carried.
37:3.reflection: Do I seek God's help while quietly ignoring what He has already told me to do?
37:3.action: Pair your prayers today with obedience: before asking God for anything, address one thing He has already asked of you.
37:3.prayer: Father, keep me from treating prayer as a substitute for obedience. I do not want to ask for Your hand while shutting my heart to Your voice. Make my asking and my living agree before You. In Jesus' name, Amen.

37:4.devotion: At this point Jeremiah was still free, moving among the people and proclaiming God's word publicly. He did not preach from a distance or in hiding; he walked among those he addressed. His ministry was ordinary and present, even when his message was unwelcome.
37:4.reflection: Am I willing to be present among people, sharing God's truth graciously, even where it may not be popular?
37:4.action: Have one genuine, grace-filled conversation today with someone about your faith or an encouraging word from Scripture.
37:4.prayer: Lord Jesus, You walked among people and spoke truth with mercy. Help me not to hide my faith or my kindness, but to live openly among others, carrying Your word with humility and love today. Amen.

37:5.devotion: The Egyptian army marched out, and the Babylonian besiegers briefly lifted their siege of Jerusalem. To many in the city, this looked like rescue. But political maneuvering and shifting armies were not the salvation God had promised; appearances of deliverance can deceive a heart that ignores His word.
37:5.reflection: When circumstances briefly improve, do I interpret them as God's answer, or do I keep seeking His voice?
37:5.action: Before celebrating a promising development today, pause and pray, asking God for wisdom about what it truly means.
37:5.prayer: All-wise God, keep me from trusting apparent rescues more than Your promises. When circumstances shift and look hopeful, anchor me in Your word rather than in appearances. Teach me to wait on You with discernment. In Jesus' name, Amen.

37:6.devotion: In the moment when Jerusalem's situation seemed to improve, God spoke again through Jeremiah. He did not leave His people to guess at events; He sent His word into the confusion. Whatever the headlines said, the Lord still had something to say to those who would listen.
37:6.reflection: Do I turn to God's word for interpretation of my circumstances, or do I trust my own reading of events?
37:6.action: When something unexpected happens today, open your Bible before drawing conclusions, and ask God what He would teach you.
37:6.prayer: Lord, thank You that You speak into changing circumstances and uncertain days. Tune my ears to Your word above every news report and every fear. Give me discernment to see my situation through Your truth. In Jesus' name, Amen.

37:7.devotion: King Zedekiah sent messengers to Jeremiah, hoping God would announce rescue. Instead, God answered honestly: Pharaoh's army, on which Judah staked its hope, would turn back to Egypt. God speaks truth even when it is unwelcome, and His word does not bend to flatter our preferred outcomes.
37:7.reflection: When I ask God for answers, am I prepared to hear truth that contradicts what I want to hear?
37:7.action: Bring one situation to God today and ask Him to show you His truth, committing in advance to accept it.
37:7.prayer: Lord, You are truthful even when Your word is hard. Give me a heart that seeks Your answer rather than my own, and grace to receive whatever You say. Amen.

37:8.devotion: God plainly warned that the Babylonians would return, capture Jerusalem, and burn it. This was not cruelty but a true warning meant to lead the king and people toward repentance and surrender to God's discipline. Hard truth, received humbly, is a mercy that gives time to respond.
37:8.reflection: Do I treat God's warnings as enemies of my peace, or as loving invitations to turn back to Him?
37:8.action: Identify one warning you have been avoiding—about a habit, relationship, or choice—and write one honest step you can take this week.
37:8.prayer: Father, thank You that Your warnings are mercy. Soften my heart to receive correction, and help me turn to You today rather than delay. Amen.

37:9.devotion: God told the people not to deceive themselves with hopeful rumors that the Babylonians would leave. Self-deception is a real danger: we can silence God's word by repeating comforting lies to ourselves. Faith is not pretending; it is trusting God's honest word, even when it costs us.
37:9.reflection: What comforting illusion might I be clinging to instead of God's truthful word right now?
37:9.action: Name one self-deception to a trusted friend or mentor today and ask them to pray with you about facing it honestly.
37:9.prayer: Lord, deliver me from deceiving myself. Anchor me in Your truth, even when it is uncomfortable, and help me trust You more than my wishful thinking. Amen.

37:10.devotion: God emphasized the certainty of His word with striking imagery: even if only wounded Babylonian soldiers remained, they would rise and burn the city. The point is not delight in destruction but that God's declared judgment cannot be outlasted or outmaneuvered. Rejecting His word does not make it go away.
37:10.reflection: Am I trying to outlast God's conviction with endurance of my own, rather than responding to Him?
37:10.action: Stop resisting one matter of obedience you have been delaying, and take the first concrete step toward it today.
37:10.prayer: Father, Your word stands, and no resistance of mine changes it. Teach me that responding to You is wiser than resisting You. Make my heart willing today. Amen.

37:11.devotion: When the Babylonian army briefly withdrew to face Pharaoh's advance, the siege lifted for a moment. This pause is the background to what follows: it seemed like relief, but God had already spoken otherwise. Circumstances can look like answers, yet only God's word tells us what is truly happening.
37:11.reflection: Do I let changing circumstances override what God has already shown me?
37:11.action: Review one situation where circumstances changed and ask God in prayer whether His direction for you has changed or not.
37:11.prayer: Lord, keep me from reading circumstances as Your voice when You have already spoken. Root me in Your word, steady when things shift around me. Amen.

37:12.devotion: During the brief lift of the siege, Jeremiah left Jerusalem to attend to property in Benjamin, likely family land matters amid the chaos. The prophet was simply carrying out an ordinary responsibility when trouble found him. Faithfulness often includes mundane duties, and doing them can bring unexpected opposition.
37:12.reflection: Am I faithful in ordinary responsibilities even when the times are uncertain?
37:12.action: Complete one practical, postponed task today—paperwork, a phone call, an errand—as an act of steady stewardship.
37:12.prayer: Father, help me be faithful in ordinary things, not only in dramatic moments. Order my daily responsibilities, and keep me steady when trouble comes. Amen.

37:13.devotion: At the city gate, Irijah the captain accused Jeremiah of defecting to the Babylonians. Because Jeremiah had urged surrender to God's word, people assumed his heart was with the enemy. Standing for God's truth can bring false accusations from those who cannot distinguish loyalty to God from betrayal of men.
37:13.reflection: When I am misunderstood for doing right, do I grow bitter, or do I keep entrusting my reputation to God?
37:13.action: If someone has misjudged you recently, release that judgment to God in prayer today instead of rehearsing it in your mind.
37:13.prayer: Lord, You know my heart when others misread it. Guard me from bitterness under false accusation, and help me keep my conscience clear before You. Amen.

37:14.devotion: Jeremiah denied the false charge plainly—"False! I am not defecting"—but Irijah would not listen, and the prophet was handed over to the officials. He spoke truth and it availed nothing with his accuser. Scripture shows that faithful people may still be unjustly treated; God's servants are not promised exemption from injustice.
37:14.reflection: Am I prepared to speak honestly and still accept outcomes I cannot control, trusting God with the result?
37:14.action: Speak one honest, gracious word today in a situation where you might otherwise stay silent or overexplain yourself.
37:14.prayer: Father, when my honest words are ignored and I am treated unfairly, keep me from despair. You see the truth; teach me to rest my case with You. Amen.

37:15.devotion: Jeremiah had spoken the word God gave him, but the princes did not want to hear it. In anger they beat him and confined him in the house of Jonathan the scribe, which had been turned into a prison. Faithful proclamation of God's truth sometimes meets hostility from those in authority.
37:15.reflection: When God's truth challenges me, do I humble myself to receive it or grow angry like these princes?
37:15.action: If someone's honest words sting you today, pause before reacting and ask God what He may be saying through them.
37:15.prayer: Father, give me a soft heart toward Your truth, even when it is uncomfortable. Keep me from striking back at those who speak honestly, and help me to listen with humility and grace today. In Jesus' name, amen.

37:16.devotion: Jeremiah remained many days in the dungeon and cells, shut away for simply speaking what God commanded. His faithful service did not spare him from prolonged confinement and isolation. Seasons of waiting in hard places are part of many believers' stories.
37:16.reflection: In my own season of confinement or delay, am I trusting God's presence or feeling abandoned by Him?
37:16.action: Reach out to someone going through a long, difficult season today with a call, visit, or note of encouragement.
37:16.prayer: Lord, You see me in the long, hard stretches when nothing seems to change. Stay near and strengthen my heart to remain faithful. Help me also remember those who feel shut in and forgotten today. In Jesus' name, amen.

37:17.devotion: King Zedekiah quietly brought Jeremiah out and asked, "Is there any word from the LORD?" Jeremiah faithfully repeated the hard message: the king would be delivered into Babylon's hand. Zedekiah wanted comfort but received truth, and Jeremiah did not soften God's word to please power.
37:17.reflection: When I ask God for a word, do I truly want His answer, or only the answer I hope to hear?
37:17.action: Bring one honest question to God today and commit, before you pray, to accept whatever He shows you in Scripture.
37:17.prayer: Lord, I want Your word more than my preferences. Give me courage to hear You clearly and obedience to follow, even when the answer is difficult. Make me truthful like Jeremiah when others only want pleasing words. Amen.

37:18.devotion: Jeremiah calmly asked the king what offense he had committed against him, his servants, or the people to deserve prison. His question exposed the injustice plainly. Speaking God's word had been treated as a crime, and Jeremiah defended himself without bitterness or retaliation.
37:18.reflection: When I face unfair treatment, do I respond with gracious honesty, or do I lash out in bitterness?
37:18.action: If you have suffered an unfair treatment recently, write a calm, truthful description of it and pray over it before deciding any next steps.
37:18.prayer: Father, when I am treated unfairly, guard my heart from bitterness. Give me Jeremiah's calm courage to speak truth about injustice without hatred. Help me trust You as my defender when others wrong me. In Jesus' name, amen.

37:19.devotion: Jeremiah reminded the king that the prophets who promised Babylon would never come had been proved false, yet Jeremiah, whose words came true, sat in prison. The contrast was stark: flattering lies had been welcomed while God's truthful word was punished.
37:19.reflection: Whose voices am I preferring—those who tell me what I want, or those who tell me God's truth?
37:19.action: Identify one trusted person who speaks God's word honestly to you, and thank them today for their faithfulness.
37:19.prayer: Lord, keep me from preferring comfortable lies to Your truth. Give me discernment to recognize faithful voices and humility to heed them. Protect Your church from flattering words, and raise up courageous, truthful messengers. In Jesus' name, amen.

37:20.devotion: Jeremiah made a humble, direct appeal to King Zedekiah: do not send me back to the house of Jonathan, lest I die there. He did not pretend suffering did not matter. He honestly named his need and asked for mercy, and his petition was reasonable and clear.
37:20.reflection: Am I willing to ask for help honestly, or do I suffer silently out of pride or fear?
37:20.action: Name one practical need you have been hiding, and ask someone you trust for help with it today.
37:20.prayer: Father, You invite us to bring our petitions honestly. Give me humility to ask for help when I need it, and wisdom to make my appeal plainly. Use others' kindness to sustain me, as You sustained Jeremiah. Amen.

37:21.devotion: Zedekiah granted only a partial relief: Jeremiah was moved to the court of the prison and given daily bread from the bakers while the city's supply lasted. He was still confined, yet God provided bread each day. Sometimes God's provision comes within limited circumstances rather than full freedom.
37:21.reflection: Can I recognize God's daily provision even while I am still waiting for full deliverance?
37:21.action: List three provisions you received today, even amid ongoing difficulties, and thank God for each one specifically.
37:21.prayer: Lord, thank You for daily bread, even when circumstances remain hard. Teach me to see Your faithful provision inside my limitations and to trust You while I wait for fuller relief. Sustain me day by day. In Jesus' name, amen.

38:1.devotion: This verse introduces four officials who heard Jeremiah's words to all the people. Their hearing would lead to opposition, as the following verses show. Jeremiah had spoken publicly, not secretly, and now powerful men were listening—some with hostile intent toward God's messenger.
38:1.reflection: When I know speaking truth may bring opposition, am I faithful to speak anyway, or does fear silence me?
38:1.action: Speak one truth God has laid on your heart today—graciously and clearly—even if it might not be popular.
38:1.prayer: Father, make me bold and gentle, speaking Your word faithfully even when powerful voices resist it. Guard my motives so I speak in love, not pride. Give me courage that does not depend on people's approval. In Jesus' name, amen.

38:2.devotion: Jeremiah delivers the LORD's message to the people of Jerusalem under siege: staying in the city means death, but surrendering to the Babylonians means life. It was a hard, humiliating word. God's mercy came wrapped in an instruction that felt like betrayal, yet it was the only path to survival.
38:2.reflection: Has God ever asked me to do something that felt like defeat but was actually obedience?
38:2.action: Consider one area where your pride resists God's direction, and write down what surrendering it might look like today.
38:2.prayer: Father, give me ears to hear Your word even when it wounds my pride. Help me trust that Your ways lead to life, even when they look like loss. Keep me from clinging to what You are calling me to release. Amen.

38:3.devotion: Jeremiah repeats the LORD's certain word: Jerusalem will fall to Babylon's army. There was no shortcut, no loophole, no political maneuver that could overturn it. Sometimes faithfulness means telling the truth about a situation even when everyone hopes for a different answer.
38:3.reflection: Am I willing to face an honest truth I have been avoiding?
38:3.action: Name one difficult reality you have been postponing, and take one small practical step to address it today.
38:3.prayer: Lord, You see what I try to avoid. Give me courage to face hard truths without despair, knowing that honesty with You is the beginning of wisdom and peace. Strengthen me to act wisely today. Amen.

38:4.devotion: The princes accuse Jeremiah of weakening morale and harming the people. Truth-tellers are often misread as troublemakers. Jeremiah sought their welfare by speaking God's word, but those in power heard only criticism. Faithful speech can be costly when it challenges what others want to believe.
38:4.reflection: When my words are unwelcome, do I still speak truth graciously?
38:4.action: Speak one needed truth kindly today, even in a small conversation, without harshness or fear of awkwardness.
38:4.prayer: Father, make me honest and gentle at the same time. Guard me from silence when You call me to speak, and from harshness when You call me to love. Let my words serve others' good, not my own vindication. Amen.

38:5.devotion: Zedekiah yields Jeremiah to his accusers, claiming he is powerless before them. The king had authority but lacked the courage to use it. His passive words handed an innocent man over to suffering. Weak leadership in the face of pressure often causes real harm to real people.
38:5.reflection: Where am I staying silent or passive when I should act with courage?
38:5.action: Identify one situation where you have deferred to pressure, and take one decisive, responsible step in it today.
38:5.prayer: Lord, deliver me from cowardice dressed up as helplessness. You give me whatever influence I have; help me use it faithfully for good. Give me backbone in moments of pressure and protect those my silence could harm. Amen.

38:6.devotion: Jeremiah is lowered by ropes into a cistern of mire and left to sink. Preaching obedience cost him his comfort, his freedom, nearly his life. Scripture does not hide the suffering of God's faithful servants; it shows endurance in the darkest, muddiest places.
38:6.reflection: When obedience brings hardship instead of comfort, will I still hold to God?
38:6.action: If you are in a muddy season, tell one trusted person honestly today and ask them to pray with you.
38:6.prayer: Father, for everyone sinking in the mire right now, be near. Remind them that hardship in faithfulness is not abandonment by You. Give me endurance in my own low places and compassion for others in theirs. Amen.

38:7.devotion: Ebed-Melech, a foreign court official, hears of Jeremiah's plight. He is an outsider in status, yet he notices what others ignore and refuses to look away. God often raises up unexpected helpers, and compassion begins simply with paying attention to someone else's suffering.
38:7.reflection: Whose suffering around me am I currently not noticing?
38:7.action: Slow down and genuinely notice one person who may be struggling, then check in with them by a call or visit today.
38:7.prayer: Lord, open my eyes today. Keep me from passing by people in trouble because they are not my kind or my concern. Make me alert to suffering and willing to be the unexpected helper someone needs. Amen.

38:8.devotion: Ebed-Melech leaves the safety of the king's house and goes directly to Zedekiah to plead for Jeremiah. He risks his standing to defend a condemned man. Courage for justice often means leaving a comfortable position to speak up where it is unpopular.
38:8.reflection: What risk keeps me from speaking up for someone who is being wronged?
38:8.action: Take one concrete advocacy step today, such as speaking to someone with authority on behalf of a person who is overlooked.
